items.title: Desktop: show owning profile for pinned sessions in All Profiles view
items.body:
## Feature description

Show the owning Hermes profile for pinned conversations when the Desktop sidebar is in **All Profiles** view.

Today the Pinned section is a flat list spanning every profile, but its rows do not identify which profile owns each conversation. The active conversation tab, composer, and status area also omit the profile. This makes it impossible to tell at a glance which agent/persona will receive the next message.

The small lead dot beside a pinned session is not a profile indicator; it represents session state such as idle, running, waiting for input, background work, or unread completion.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two or more Hermes profiles.
2. Create conversations under different profiles.
3. Pin at least one conversation from each profile.
4. Select **All Profiles** using the profile rail.
5. Open a conversation from the flat Pinned section.

## Current behavior

- Pinned rows display the session title and status dot only.
- No profile name, initial, color badge, or profile tooltip appears on the row.
- The open session tab/header and composer do not show the owning profile.
- The only reliable workarounds are `/profile`, filtering profiles one at a time, or temporarily unpinning the conversation so it appears under a grouped profile section.

## Proposed behavior

When **All Profiles** is selected:

- Show the owning profile's configured color and initial on each pinned session row.
- Include `Profile: <name>` in the row tooltip or accessible label.
- Keep the session-status indicator separate from profile identity.
- Show the profile in the active session tab or header, for example: `Meeting Summaries #3 · Xavier`.
- Use text or an accessible label in addition to color.
- Avoid redundant profile badges in single-profile or profile-filtered views.

## Motivation

Profiles isolate configuration, memory, skills, sessions, credentials, and personas. Sending a message to the wrong profile can therefore change behavior materially. Pinned conversations remove the grouped profile context that otherwise communicates ownership in All Profiles view.

## Suggested implementation areas

- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-row.tsx`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/index.tsx`
- Active session tab/header component

Please add Desktop tests covering pinned sessions from multiple profiles and preserve the existing status-dot semantics.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop: 0.18.2 +8
- OS: macOS 15.6
- Multiple named profiles with All Profiles view enabled

items.title: Hermes Desktop "Read aloud" times out on long replies (15s fetch timeout — regression)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary
In Hermes Desktop, clicking **Read aloud** on a longer assistant reply fails with:

> **Read aloud failed** — Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms

Short replies read aloud fine; only replies whose TTS takes more than ~15s to synthesize fail. This looks like a regression introduced with the recent auto-speak / read-aloud work.

## Environment
- Hermes Desktop **0.17.0** (macOS, Apple Silicon)
- TTS provider: `xai` (voice `ara`)
- Backend: local Hermes gateway

## Steps to reproduce
1. Set the TTS provider to xAI (`ara`) in `config.yaml`.
2. Get a long assistant reply (long enough that speech synthesis takes >15s).
3. Click **Read aloud**.
4. After 15s: *"Read aloud failed — Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms."*

## Expected vs. actual
- **Expected:** Read aloud waits long enough for the audio to synthesize (the backend's own xAI TTS request already allows 60s).
- **Actual:** The desktop client aborts the request at 15s, before the audio returns.

## Root cause (from the source)
The read-aloud request uses the app's **generic default fetch timeout**, not a TTS-appropriate one:

- `apps/desktop/electron/hardening.ts`: `const DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`
- The read-aloud fetch resolves its timeout via `resolveTimeoutMs(options.timeoutMs, DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS)` and passes no explicit value, so it falls back to 15s.
- `resolveTimeoutMs` reads **no environment or config override** — only an explicit per-call value or the 15s fallback. So there's no user-side setting to work around it.

## Why this looks like a regression
The auto-speak / read-aloud feature and its wiring to the generic 15s fetch timeout are all recent (roughly late June – mid July 2026): the auto-speak watcher hook, the `useComposerVoice` engine extraction, the TypeScript refactor that introduced `DEFAULT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`, and the chat-view/composer integration. The failures began right after these landed.

## Suggested fix
Give the TTS / read-aloud fetch path its own timeout, well above the backend's TTS ceiling:
- Pass an explicit `timeoutMs` (e.g. **60–120s**) on the read-aloud request, **or**
- Make the default configurable via env/setting (e.g. `HERMES_DESKTOP_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`).

The backend's xAI TTS request already allows 60s (`tools/tts_tool.py` → `_generate_xai_tts`, `timeout=60`), so the desktop client should wait at least that long for the read-aloud response.

## Note on local workarounds
There's no practical user-side workaround: the value is compiled into the packaged app, and the shipped `app.asar` is integrity-protected (`ElectronAsarIntegrity` in `Info.plist`), so patching the built bundle isn't viable without rebuilding and re-signing. A fix in the app itself is needed.

items.title: [Bug]: Hermes Desktop ignores per-profile tts/voice config; always uses global/default TTS provider

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
# [Bug]: Hermes Desktop ignores per-profile `tts:`/`voice:` config; always uses global/default TTS provider

## Component
Desktop

## Environment
- **OS:** Windows 11 Pro
- **Hermes:** Desktop app
- **Model/provider:** stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free via Nous
- **Config path:** `C:\Users\Marti\AppData\Local\hermes\config.yaml`
- **Profile under test:** `selene` (`C:\Users\Marti\AppData\Local\hermes\profiles\selene\config.yaml`)

## Summary
When the Hermes desktop app runs with a non-default profile (`selene`), it does **not** apply that profile's `tts:` / `voice:` configuration for voice output. Instead, it falls back to the global/default profile's TTS provider. The CLI **does** honor the profile-specific config correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a profile named `selene` under `~/.hermes/profiles/selene/config.yaml` with:
   ```yaml
   tts:
     provider: piper
     piper:
       voice: en_GB-alba-medium
   voice:
     auto_tts: true
     provider: piper
   ```
2. Set the main `config.yaml` to a different TTS provider, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   tts:
     provider: edge
     edge:
       voice: en-GB-RyanNeural
   ```
3. In the Hermes desktop app, switch to the **selene** profile.
4. Trigger TTS output (e.g., `/voice on`, or any auto-TTS response).
5. Observe that the desktop app still uses **Edge TTS** instead of **Piper**.

## Expected Behavior
The desktop app should load and use the active profile's `tts:` and `voice:` settings for audio generation, matching the CLI behavior.

## Actual Behavior
- **CLI:** When run with the `selene` profile, audio is generated with Piper (`provider: piper`) as configured in the profile.
- **Desktop:** Even though the backend reports `profile: "selene"`, `agent.log` shows TTS is still generated with Edge TTS (`provider: edge`), ignoring the profile's config entirely.

## Log Evidence
From `C:\Users\Marti\AppData\Local\hermes\logs\desktop.log`:
```text
[hermes] Starting Hermes backend for profile "selene" via Hermes at ...
```

From `C:\Users\Marti\AppData\Local\hermes\logs\agent.log`:
```text
INFO tools.tts_tool: Generating speech with Edge TTS...
INFO tools.tts_tool: TTS audio saved: ... provider: edge
```

This happens **after** switching to the selene profile in the desktop app, confirming the desktop surface is not routing TTS through the profile config.

## Additional Context
- `piper.exe` is installed in the Hermes venv at `C:\Users\Marti\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\piper.exe`.
- Piper voice files for `en_GB-alba-medium` exist in `C:\Users\Marti\AppData\Local\hermes\cache\piper-voices\`.
- Main `config.yaml` has no YAML errors.
- The issue is isolated to the **desktop app**. Profile isolation works in the CLI.

## Suggested Fix Area
The desktop app/backend appears to read the profile name for session isolation but may not be wiring the profile-specific config into the TTS dispatch path. Investigation should focus on:
1. Desktop profile switching and config reload logic
2. Where the desktop surface resolves `tts.provider` / `voice.provider`
3. Whether `voice.*` and `tts.*` from `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/config.yaml` are merged/applied in desktop mode

items.title: hermes -z (oneshot) silently ignores terminal.backend and executes tools with the local backend — sandbox bypass

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Summary

`hermes -z` (oneshot) **silently ignores `terminal.backend`** and runs every terminal-tool call with the **local** backend, in-process, regardless of what the user configured. A user who set `terminal.backend: ssh` (or `docker`/`daytona`/`modal`) specifically to sandbox tool execution gets oneshot commands executed **directly in the host/container environment with no warning and no error** — the isolation they configured is silently bypassed.

This is the security-relevant sibling of the terminal-config-bridge issues already tracked (#28892 bridge drift, #29239 "config.yaml authoritative for terminal.backend", #61882 "fail closed when the bridge is unavailable"): those cover the bridge being *wrong* or *unavailable*; this is the bridge being **never invoked at all** on the oneshot path, which fails **open** to local.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.18.2** (`2026.7.7.2`, upstream `bb5fc723`)
- Python 3.11.15, Linux (Fedora), podman container
- `config.yaml`: `terminal.backend: ssh` (tool execution meant to run in an isolated SSH sandbox VM)
- Confirmed still present on `main`: `hermes_cli/oneshot.py` contains **no** `TERMINAL_ENV` / config-bridge reference, and `hermes_cli/main.py` dispatches oneshot via `_prepare_agent_startup(args)` → `run_oneshot(...)`, neither of which applies the terminal bridge.

### Root cause

The config→env bridge that maps `terminal.backend` to `TERMINAL_ENV` (which `tools/terminal_tool.py` actually reads — it defaults to `"local"` when the var is unset) lives in **two** places, and **both are on paths the oneshot never takes**:

- `cli.py` `load_cli_config()` — runs at `import cli` (`CLI_CONFIG = load_cli_config()`), i.e. the interactive CLI/TUI path.
- `gateway/run.py` — the gateway's own bridge block.

The oneshot dispatch (`main.py`: `if getattr(args, "oneshot", ...)` → `_prepare_agent_startup(args)` → `run_oneshot()`) **bypasses `cli.py` entirely** (as `oneshot.py`'s own docstring states: *"Bypasses cli.py entirely."*) and does not run the gateway bridge either. So `TERMINAL_ENV` is never set from config, `terminal_tool` sees it empty, and falls back to `local`.

### Reproduction

With `terminal.backend: ssh` configured and working (verified below), from inside the same container:

**1. Oneshot — reads empty `TERMINAL_ENV`, runs locally:**
```console
$ hermes -z "Run with the terminal tool: cat /etc/hostname; echo USER=$(whoami); echo TERMINAL_ENV=$TERMINAL_ENV — reply with only the raw output."
4ceb3b8ccccb          # <-- the hermes container's own hostname
USER=hermes           # <-- the container user, NOT the sandbox
TERMINAL_ENV=         # <-- empty: the bridge never ran
```

**2. Same container, with the bridge applied (`import cli` runs `load_cli_config()`) — routes to the SSH sandbox as configured:**
```console
$ python -c "import cli; from tools.terminal_tool import terminal_tool; print(terminal_tool('hostname && whoami'))"
{"output": "fedora\nsandbox", "exit_code": 0, "error": null}   # <-- the sandbox VM
```

Identical config, identical command, opposite execution environment — the only difference is whether the terminal bridge ran. Oneshot is the branch where it doesn't.

### Impact

- **Sandbox bypass (security):** the entire point of a non-local `terminal.backend` is to keep model-driven shell execution off the host. Oneshot defeats that silently. `hermes -z` is exactly the mode people wire into scripts, cron, and CI — unattended contexts where a silent fallback to local execution is worst-case.
- **Silent, not fail-loud:** no warning, no error, exit code 0. The user has no signal that isolation was dropped.
- **Consistency:** interactive chat, TUI, and gateway sessions all honor `terminal.backend`; only oneshot doesn't, so the same config behaves differently depending on entry point.

### Suggested direction

Apply the terminal config bridge on the oneshot path before the agent runs — ideally by extracting the bridge into a single shared helper both `cli.py`/`gateway/run.py` and `run_oneshot()` call (this would also close the 3-dict drift noted in #28892). Per the #61882 precedent, if a non-local backend is configured but cannot be initialized in the oneshot context, oneshot should **fail closed** (error out) rather than fall back to local. Happy to put up a PR along these lines if the approach sounds right.

items.title: [Feature]: Context-Aware Orchestrator Model Routing — Agent self-routes tasks to optimal models

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Problem Statement

Hermes Agent currently locks each session to a single model via `config.yaml`. To use different models for different tasks (e.g., a cheap fast model for casual chat, a powerful coding model for implementation work), the user must either:

1. Manually switch models via `/model` slash command every time the context changes
2. Use `delegate_task` subagents, which breaks conversational flow
3. Run separate profiles for different use cases

This makes Hermes a single-model agent rather than an **intelligent orchestration layer** that can route tasks to the best model for the job automatically.

When a user asks "What is the weather today?" vs "Write a React component with TypeScript", the same model processes both — wasting cost on simple queries and potentially underperforming on complex ones.

---

## Proposed Solution

### Core Concept: Agent Self-Routing

The primary agent (not a subagent, not a manual command) should be able to **self-identify the nature of each user request** and route it to the most suitable model automatically — all within the same conversational session.

The routing is:
- **Transparent** — the user just asks, the agent picks the right tool (model) for the job
- **Contextual** — based on the actual content of the conversation, not predefined task types
- **Stateless** — each model swap is clean; tool calls, history, and agent state remain coherent

### Configuration Example

```yaml
model_routing:
  enabled: true
  default: deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash  # fallback for everything else
  routes:
    - match: ["coding", "implementation", "code_review", "debugging"]
      model: qwen/qwen3-235b-a75b
    - match: ["planning", "architecture", "analysis"]
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4
    - match: ["vision", "screenshot", "ui_analysis"]
      model: nvidia/nemotron-nano-12b-v2-vl
    - match: ["chat", "casual", "quick_answer"]
      model: meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free
```

### How It Works

1. **Detection**: The agent's system prompt includes a routing map. At the start of each turn, the agent analyzes the user's message + recent context and determines the task category (coding, chat, planning, vision, etc.)
2. **Routing**: If the detected category differs from the current model, the agent issues an internal routing request. The framework handles the model swap transparently and continues within the same conversation
3. **Continuity**: Message history, tool call results, and agent state persist across model switches. The user sees a seamless experience
4. **Fallback**: If no route matches, or if the routed model fails, fall back to the default model

### Detection Approaches

**Option A — Agent self-identifies (preferred)**  
The agent's system prompt includes the routing rules and is instructed to classify each incoming message. This is the most flexible approach — the agent understands subtle context.

**Option B — Lightweight classifier**  
A small, fast classification model pre-classifies the message before passing it to the main agent. The classifier itself routes to the appropriate model.

**Option C — Hybrid**  
Agent classifies, but has a `route_task(category)` internal tool as a fallback for explicit routing.

---

## Use Cases

| Scenario | Current UX | With Routing |
|:---|---:|:---|
| Morning briefing + code review in same session | Manually /model switch twice | Agent auto-routes: briefing to fast model, code to coding model |
| Casual chat to suddenly debugging | Stick with expensive model or switch manually | Agent detects debugging context, routes to coding model automatically |
| Multi-step planning + implementation | Suboptimal single model for both phases | Planning to reasoning model, Implementation to coding model |
| Vision task mid-conversation | Cannot use without separate profile | Agent detects image input, routes to vision-capable model |

---

## Relationship to Existing Issues

This proposal differs from:

- **#4461 (Multimodel Routing for Profiles)**: That proposal focuses on predefined static task-category to model mapping in config. This proposal adds **agent self-awareness** — the agent dynamically classifies and routes based on conversation context.
- **#5508 (Per-skill model routing)**: Skill-level routing only works when `delegate_task(skill=...)` is called. The main agent remains single-model. This proposal makes the **main agent itself multi-model**.
- **#38954 (Role-Based Routing)**: Focuses on a fixed planning to coding to review pipeline. This proposal is freeform — any task type, any time, based on actual user input.
- **#157 (Capability Categories)**: More about tool-level model requests. This proposal is about the **orchestrator** (the agent) making routing decisions.

---

## Impact

- **Backward compatible** — when `model_routing.enabled: false` (default), behavior is identical to today
- **Zero user friction** — works out of the box once configured; no slash commands, no manual switches
- **Cost efficient** — cheap models for simple queries, powerful models only when needed
- **Future-proof** — new models can be added to routes without changing agent behavior

---

## Suggested Scope

This is a **medium-to-large feature** requiring changes in:
- `config.yaml` schema (new `model_routing` block)
- Agent runtime (`run_agent.py` or a new `model_router.py` module)
- System prompt builder (inject routing rules)
- Context management (clean model swaps)

However, the core logic is conceptually simple: classify → route → continue.

items.title: feat: /branch should open a new thread on Discord/Telegram/Slack

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Problem

`/branch` (aka `/fork`) clones the session transcript but rebinds the **same** chat/thread surface to the clone. On Discord (and similar thread-capable platforms) that abandons the original conversation on that surface — you cannot keep chatting on the original path in-thread while exploring the branch elsewhere without manually `/resume`.

Users often want the opposite default for threaded platforms: explore the branch in a **sibling thread**, leave this surface on the original session.

## Proposal

| Surface | `/branch` | `/branch --here [name]` |
|---------|-----------|-------------------------|
| Discord / Telegram / Slack | Clone + open **new** thread; origin stays | Clone on **current** surface (old behavior) |
| WhatsApp / CLI / others | In-place (no threads) | In-place |

Reuse existing `adapter.create_handoff_thread` (already used by CLI handoff + cron attach). Match Discord inbound session-key shape so replies land on the clone.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Discord: `/branch` from a channel/thread creates a new thread with cloned history; original stays put
- [ ] Discord: `/branch --here` switches the current surface onto the clone (legacy)
- [ ] Non-thread platforms: `/branch` still in-place; never treats flags as titles
- [ ] Tests cover parse, Discord default thread, `--here`, WhatsApp in-place

## Notes

Related PR will implement this. Soft-fall back to in-place when parent channel is missing (e.g. pure DMs).

items.title: Windows: agent turn hangs forever in the git workspace probe when the 2.5s timeout fires (post-kill communicate deadlock)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## What happens

On Windows, when the git probe in `agent/coding_context.py` (`_git`, called from `build_coding_workspace_block`) hits its 2.5s timeout, the whole agent turn hangs forever. The prompt is received, `agent.turn_context` logs the turn start, and then nothing — no model call, no updates, no error. From the outside it looks like the model is thinking indefinitely.

Hit this while driving `hermes acp` (0.18.2) embedded in another app on Windows 11, with the process cwd inside a large git repo (git status legitimately exceeds 2.5s there).

## py-spy stack of the wedged turn

```
Thread "acp-agent_0"
    _wait_for_tstate_lock (threading.py:1139)
    join (threading.py:1119)
    _communicate (subprocess.py:1628)
    communicate (subprocess.py:1209)
    run (subprocess.py:559)          <- TimeoutExpired handler's cleanup communicate()
    _git (agent/coding_context.py:694)
    build_coding_workspace_block (agent/coding_context.py:858)
    ...
    build_turn_context -> run_conversation -> acp_adapter/server.py:1513
```

git itself was already dead at this point (no git child under the process tree).

## Why

`subprocess.run()`'s `TimeoutExpired` handler on Windows kills the child and then calls `process.communicate()` **with no timeout** to collect remaining output. That relies on the pipes reaching EOF. If any other process was spawned concurrently by another thread — an MCP server child, another probe — it can inherit duplicates of the pipe handles (the well-known CPython Windows concurrent-Popen inheritance race), so the pipes never EOF even though git is gone, and the reader-thread join blocks forever. An agent host that registers MCP servers at session start and prompts right after makes this race easy to hit: the git probe runs exactly while those long-lived children are starting.

## Repro sketch

Windows 11, cwd = a large git repo (so `git status --porcelain=2 --branch` exceeds `_GIT_TIMEOUT=2.5`), an ACP session with at least one MCP server configured, prompt immediately after `session/new`. In my environment this wedged 5 out of 5 attempts; adding an artificial delay between session creation and the first prompt (letting the MCP children finish starting) made it pass, which is what pointed at the spawn race rather than git itself.

## Fix

Bound the post-kill cleanup instead of relying on pipe EOF — PR incoming: `_git` switched to `Popen` + explicit `communicate(timeout)` + a bounded (1s) post-kill `communicate`, abandoning the pipes after the grace period. Also sets `stdin=DEVNULL` so a git that decides to prompt can't wait on input. Normal-path behavior unchanged.

items.title: install.sh + setup with camofox provider: post-setup crashes on missing source dir, leaves no working hermes install

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

Running the official install.sh on a Linux host and choosing **camofox** as the browser provider during `hermes setup` crashes with `FileNotFoundError: '/home/<user>/.hermes/hermes-agent'`. The crash happens *after* the installer has deleted a pre-existing source checkout at that path but *before* it has installed hermes via `uv tool install`, leaving the user with no working `hermes` binary at all.

Two related issues:

1. **Path assumption mismatch.** `_run_post_setup` for camofox assumes a source checkout exists at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` (it subprocess-runs something from that directory). The install.sh path installs via `uv tool install`, which does not create that directory — it puts the package under `~/.local/share/uv/tools/`. So the post-setup step always crashes on a uv-based install when camofox is selected.

2. **Uninstall is not crash-safe.** install.sh deletes any pre-existing `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` source checkout *before* the new install succeeds. If anything later in the wizard crashes (as it did here), the user is left with neither the old install nor a new one. `uv tool list` shows nothing; `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` is gone.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a Linux host, have an existing source-based install at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` (git clone + venv + `pip install -e .`).
2. Run `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash`.
3. Proceed through `hermes setup`. When prompted for browser automation, choose `camofox`.
4. Accept the default server URL (`http://localhost:9377`).

## Expected Behavior

- Camofox post-setup should not depend on a source checkout at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` when hermes was installed via `uv tool install`.
- install.sh should not remove the previous install before the new one is verified working (or should restore on failure).

## Actual Behavior

Traceback (abridged):

```
File ".../hermes_cli/setup.py", line 2198, in setup_tools
File ".../hermes_cli/tools_config.py", line 4086, in tools_command
File ".../hermes_cli/tools_config.py", line 2217, in _configure_toolset
File ".../hermes_cli/tools_config.py", line 2784, in _configure_tool_category
File ".../hermes_cli/tools_config.py", line 3477, in _configure_provider
File ".../hermes_cli/tools_config.py", line 1288, in _run_post_setup
File ".../python3.12/subprocess.py", line 548, in run
    with Popen(*popenargs, **kwargs) as process:
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/home/computing/.hermes/hermes-agent'
```

After the crash:
- `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` no longer exists (deleted by install.sh)
- `uv tool list` shows "No tools installed"
- No `hermes` binary on PATH — user must reinstall from scratch

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu (Linux x86_64)
- Python: 3.12.13 (via uv)
- Hermes version being installed: v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), upstream 56e2ba5e
- Install method attempted: install.sh (uv tool install path)
- Browser provider chosen during setup: camofox

items.title: Codex transport emits an over-length `prompt_cache_key` (>64) → every openai-codex request 400s and silently falls back

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
**Repo:** NousResearch/hermes-agent · **Version:** 0.18.2 (commit `2ccfdb2`)
**File:** `agent/transports/codex.py` (`_CodexResponsesTransport.build_kwargs`, ~line 267)

## Summary

On the `openai-codex` provider (ChatGPT/Codex backend, `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`), hermes can send a `prompt_cache_key` longer than 64 characters. The backend rejects any `prompt_cache_key` over 64 chars with **HTTP 400 BadRequestError**, so the codex request fails on *every* turn and hermes silently falls back to the next provider in the fallback chain. Because the failure is masked by the fallback, the primary provider looks "unused" and the true cause only surfaces if/when the fallback itself fails (e.g. OpenRouter credit/quota).

## Root cause

```python
# agent/transports/codex.py, build_kwargs()
cache_key = _content_cache_key(instructions, response_tools) or session_id
if not is_github_responses and not is_xai_responses and cache_key:
    kwargs["prompt_cache_key"] = cache_key
```

`_content_cache_key` returns a short `pck_<sha256[:24]>` when there is static content to hash, but falls back to the **raw `session_id`** otherwise. There is no length guard. When a caller supplies a long `session_id`, it is forwarded verbatim as `prompt_cache_key` and the OpenAI backend 400s.

## Concrete reproduction

Paperclip (`@paperclipai/server`) hands hermes a session id of the form
`paperclip:company:<uuid>:agent:<uuid>` — **97 chars**. Every `openai-codex`
request then fails:

```
agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=BadRequestError
  provider=openai-codex base_url=https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex model=gpt-5.6-sol
  summary=HTTP 400: Invalid 'prompt_cache_key': string too long.
          Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 97 instead.
agent.chat_completion_helpers: Fallback activated: gpt-5.6-sol → anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 (openrouter)
```

Credentials are valid; the model is accepted; only the `prompt_cache_key` length is the problem. Nothing in the surfaced error points at the primary provider being the cause — it just silently degrades to the fallback.

## Why it matters

- Silent, total loss of the primary provider on any integration that passes a session id longer than 64 chars.
- The symptom only becomes visible when the fallback also fails, which points debugging in the wrong direction (credentials / subscription / the fallback provider).

## Proposed fix

Cap/hash the key to ≤64 chars at the chokepoint. `prompt_cache_key` is a routing hint only (never a correctness boundary — matching the existing code comment), so hashing an over-length key is safe:

```python
cache_key = _content_cache_key(instructions, response_tools) or session_id
if cache_key and len(cache_key) > 64:
    cache_key = f"pck_{hashlib.sha256(cache_key.encode('utf-8', 'replace')).hexdigest()[:24]}"
```

(`hashlib` is already imported in this module.) This defends against any caller regardless of session-id length or format.

## Environment

- hermes-agent 0.18.2 (commit `2ccfdb2`), editable install
- provider `openai-codex`, model `gpt-5.6-sol`, `api_mode=codex_responses`
- macOS (Darwin), Python 3.11, run under the hermes gateway (`hermes_cli.main gateway run`)

items.title: [Bug]: Gateway queued follow-up delivers intentional-silence markers

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug description

When a successful gateway turn returns an exact intentional-silence marker such as `[SILENT]` or `NO_REPLY` while another message is queued for the same session, the queued-follow-up fallback can deliver the marker literally before processing the next message.

This is a core gateway delivery-path issue, not a platform-specific adapter or plugin issue.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable gateway streaming.
2. Start a turn whose successful agent result and stream content are exactly `[SILENT]`.
3. Queue a second `MessageEvent` for the same session before the first `_run_agent` invocation unwinds.
4. Observe the first turn's marker being sent directly before the queued turn is processed.

A deterministic gateway regression test reproduces this with a fake two-turn agent and the real stream-consumer/queued-message path.

## Expected behavior

The intentional-silence marker remains in the agent result/transcript but is not delivered to the chat. The queued follow-up is then processed normally.

## Actual behavior

The stream consumer suppresses the marker, but the queued-follow-up fallback sends it through `adapter.send()` because final stream delivery was not confirmed.

The relevant log line is:

```text
Queued follow-up for session ...: final stream delivery not confirmed; sending first response before continuing.
```

The user then sees a literal `[SILENT]` message.

## Root cause

`GatewayStreamConsumer._suppress_silence_marker()` correctly leaves `final_response_sent`, `final_content_delivered`, and `already_sent` false because nothing was delivered.

The queued-follow-up branch in `gateway/run.py` interprets that false delivery state as a reason to send the first response directly:

```python
_already_streamed = _stream_confirmed_final_delivery(...)
if first_response and not _already_streamed:
    await adapter.send(..., first_response, ...)
```

That direct-send path runs inside `_run_agent`, before the normal whole-response filter in `_handle_message_with_agent`, so it bypasses `is_intentional_silence_agent_result()`.

The branch currently conflates two different states:

- the response was not delivered and still needs delivery;
- the response was intentionally suppressed and must never be delivered.

## Proposed fix

Apply the existing canonical `is_intentional_silence_agent_result(result, first_response)` predicate in the queued-follow-up branch before delivery-confirmation fallback logic.

If it is an intentional-silence result, skip `adapter.send()` and continue processing the queued message. Do not mutate the result/transcript, mark the response as delivered, or add platform-specific filtering.

This preserves the existing contracts:

- only successful exact whole-response markers are suppressed;
- failed agent results are not hidden;
- substantive prose mentioning `[SILENT]` or `NO_REPLY` is delivered normally;
- all gateway platforms share the same behavior.

## Regression evidence

Without the queue guard, the integration test captures:

```python
['[SILENT]', 'follow-up response']
```

With the guard, the follow-up is delivered and `[SILENT]` is absent.

The prepared regression and the existing whole-response/streaming suites pass: **77 tests passed** on Python 3.11 with the locked `all + dev` dependency set. Ruff, diff checks, and the Windows-footgun checker also pass.

## Related issue

- #55806 reports the same queued fallback resending a response whose real delivery was not represented by the stream consumer. This issue is distinct: the response was intentionally suppressed, so it must not be treated as delivered or retried.

A tested local patch is ready; I can submit it as a focused PR if maintainers would like one.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: `0.18.2`
- Also reproduced against `main` at `7cb2d2cd4acf0c452349968ce8d90908e8fb4cd9`
- Gateway platform observed: Telegram group
- Streaming: enabled

items.body:
hermes-bug-report.md
Bug Report: Hermes Desktop - Model Selector Dropdown Selectable But Doesn't Apply
Description
In the Hermes desktop application (v0.18.2, Windows 10), the model selector dropdown in all profile chat windows loads the model list correctly but selection does not change the actual model being used. After selecting a different model from the dropdown, the chat continues using the previously selected model with no error message, no visual indication of change, and no effect.

Affected Profiles
default (model: LongCat-2.0 via custom:longcat)
finance (model: general-moa)
history (model: deepseek-v4-flash via deepseek)
law (model: deepseek-v4-flash via deepseek)
Reproduction
Open Hermes desktop
Select any profile with any model configuration
In the chat window, click the model selector dropdown at the right side
Select any model from the dropdown list
Send a new message to the chat
Observed: The model does not change; it continues using the previously selected model
Expected Behavior
After selecting a model from the dropdown, the UI should:

Display the newly selected model in the status bar
Route all subsequent messages through the selected model
Optionally show a confirmation or transition indicator
Actual Behavior
Model selector dropdown shows and contains the correct full model list
Clicking a model in the dropdown updates the displayed selection momentarily
However, the actual model in use does not change — subsequent messages go through the original model
No error messages appear
The UI appears to have selected something but the backend session state never changes
Environment
OS: Windows 10 (192.168.1.99, WillP)
Hermes Version: v0.18.2 (2026-7.7.2), upstream 7cb2d2cd
Install method: git (C:\Users\WillP\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent)
Profile configs verified: interface: gui, all profiles, deepseek provider working (API connectivity confirmed)
Python: 3.11.15
OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0
Technical Analysis
This bug appears to be in the Electron UI render layer, not the application/backend configuration layer. Specifically:

model_catalog loads correctly — the dropdown is populated with the full model list including all providers (openrouter, zai, deepseek, minimax-cn, custom:longcat, etc.)
Display/frontend components are functional — the dropdown can expand and show models
State synchronization fails — the UI selection event does not propagate to the session state manager
All profiles affected — this is a systematic bug in the desktop application, not a per-profile configuration issue
Ruled-Out Causes
display.interface: cli was temporarily set (now reverted to gui) — no effect on this specific bug
model_catalog.json cache corruption — clearing cache and restart does not fix the issue
Profile configuration inconsistencies — all 4 profiles have been synced and verified; bug persists
Multiple Hermes processes causing SQLite contention — reduced to single process; bug persists
API key missing or provider errors — zap, custom:longcat, minimax-cn all respond correctly when tested via CLI hermes chat -m ...
CLI Workaround (Functional)
The command-line interface correctly switches models:

hermes chat -m glm-4.7 --provider zai --profile law
hermes chat -m deepseek-v4-flash --provider deepseek --profile law
hermes chat -m MiniMax-M3 --provider minimax-cn --profile law
This confirms that:

All providers work correctly
All API keys are valid
Model configurations are valid
The issue is isolated to the desktop UI event handling
Severity
High — Model switching is a core feature of the desktop application. Users who cannot switch models are effectively locked into their current configuration. This is especially problematic for multi-model workflows where different tasks require different models.

Additional Context
User has been experiencing this since approximately July 15, 2026
Multiple Hermes desktop restarts and config changes have not resolved the issue
On 2026-07-16, the user was told to use the CLI workaround as a permanent solution but the desktop UI bug remains unfixed
Related
fallback_models only lists 3 of 8 available Z.AI models (glm-5.2, glm-5, glm-4-9b) — dropdown shows these but not others like glm-4.7 which is available via API. This may contribute to user confusion but is not the cause of the selection-apply failure.

items.title: [Bug]: Docker-backed gateway silently drops MEDIA attachments for container-local /workspace paths

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

When the terminal backend is `docker`, the agent writes its artifact inside the sandbox container and then naturally reports the path it wrote to, either as an explicit directive (`MEDIA:/workspace/chart.png`) or as a bare path in the reply text. MEDIA delivery runs in the **gateway process on the host**, where `/workspace/...` does not exist, so `validate_media_delivery_path` fails `resolve(strict=True)` and the attachment is silently dropped. The user sees the reply text ("here you go:") with **no attachment and no error**.

The gateway already knows about this failure mode, `gateway/run.py` prints at startup:

```
WARNING gateway.run: Docker backend is enabled for the messaging gateway but no explicit host-visible output mount ... is configured. This is fine if the model already emits host-visible paths, but MEDIA file delivery can fail for container-local paths like '/workspace/...' or '/output/...'.
```

but there is no mechanism to make container paths deliverable. Prompting the model (via skill instructions) to translate `/workspace/...` into the host path itself is unreliable in practice, in our deployment the model skipped the translation on roughly half of runs even with the instruction spelled out and a helper that prints the exact host path to paste. An instruction is not a mechanism; the boundary should do the translation.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a messaging gateway (Discord in our case) with `terminal.backend: docker` (sandboxed agent, `/workspace` bind-mounted to a host dir).
2. Ask the bot to produce a file, e.g. "draw a diagram and send it as png". The agent writes `/workspace/chart.png` in its container and replies with `MEDIA:/workspace/chart.png`.
3. Watch gateway.log.

### Expected Behavior

The file, which exists on the host at `<host-workspace-mount>/chart.png`, attaches to the reply.

### Actual Behavior

```
WARNING gateway.platforms.base: Skipping unsafe MEDIA directive path: /workspace/chart.png
```

The reply posts with no attachment and no user-visible error, even though the artifact exists on the host under the workspace mount.

### Proposed fix

An opt-in env `MEDIA_WORKSPACE_HOST_ROOT` naming the host directory that backs the container's `/workspace` mount. When set, both delivery routes (`validate_media_delivery_path` for `MEDIA:` directives, `extract_local_files` for bare paths) remap the fixed `/workspace/` prefix onto it. The remapped path is realpath-fenced inside the mount, must exist, and still passes the full delivery validation (denylist / strict-mode allowlist / recency) afterwards, so the remap grants no new reach. Unset ⇒ behaviour unchanged. PR with tests to follow.

items.title: fix(mcp): catch SDK TaskGroup BaseExceptionGroup and reconnect immediately instead of backoff/park
items.body:
## Problem

Streamable‑HTTP MCP servers that experience a transient SSE stream drop (e.g. idle timeout, brief backend blip) trigger a full session teardown, exponential‑backoff reconnect, and tool deregistration — even though the POST request path is still functional.

### Root cause chain

1. The Python MCP SDK (`mcp.client.streamable_http`) runs a background GET SSE stream inside a TaskGroup.
2. When the SSE stream drops (network hiccup, idle timeout, server‑side TCP close), one of the TaskGroup's child tasks raises.
3. The SDK catches ordinary `Exception` inside `handle_get_stream()` and retries (up to 2 attempts), but any unhandled exception — or a `CancelledError` from sibling‑task cancellation — escapes as a `BaseExceptionGroup`.
4. This `BaseExceptionGroup` propagates out of `streamable_http_client()` into `_run_http()`, which exits both the `ClientSession` and `streamable_http_client` context managers.
5. The exception reaches `run()`'s `except Exception` handler, which sets `self.session = None`, increments `_reconnect_retries`, applies exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 4s → 8s → 16s), and on exhaustion *parks* the server for 300s after deregistering all tools.

**Result:** A ~50ms SSE stream glitch causes MCP tools to be unavailable for seconds to minutes, even though the server is perfectly reachable via HTTP POST.

## Location

**`tools/mcp_tool.py`** — `_run_http()` method (both the new and deprecated API branches at lines ~2500 and ~2532).

Currently the inner `async with streamable_http_client(...) / ClientSession(...)` blocks are unwrapped: any exception from the SDK's TaskGroup propagates directly into `run()`'s error‑handling path.

## Fix

Wrap the transport‑layer `async with` blocks inside `_run_http()` with a `try/except BaseExceptionGroup` that catches the SDK's TaskGroup failure and returns `"reconnect"` — the same code path used for OAuth recovery and manual `/mcp` refresh.

```python
# Line ~2500 (new API branch):
try:
    async with streamable_http_client(url, http_client=http_client) as (...):
        async with ClientSession(read_stream, write_stream, ...) as session:
            ...
            reason = await self._wait_for_lifecycle_event()
            if reason == "reconnect":
                logger.info(...)
except BaseExceptionGroup:
    logger.debug(
        "MCP server '%s': SDK transport TaskGroup exited "
        "(will auto-reconnect immediately)", self.name,
    )
    reason = "reconnect"
```

The outer `run()` loop sees `"reconnect"` — resets retry counters, clears `_ready`, and immediately re‑enters `_run_http()` to establish a fresh transport. No backoff, no parking, no tool deregistration.

## Impact

**Medium.** Affects every Streamable‑HTTP MCP server (the most common transport). Without the fix, any SSE‑stream disruption cascades into multi‑minute MCP tool outages. With the fix, the transport self‑heals in under one second and tools never drop off.

## Related

- Python SDK issue #2114 — `ExceptionGroup` wrapping obscures real errors (root cause at SDK level)
- Python SDK PR #2245 — open P1 fix for the SDK's TaskGroup error handling
- Hermes #38488 — permanent‑give‑up bug (same family, fixed independently)

items.title: Auto-extend _PROVIDER_PREFIXES from registered provider profiles (plugin providers don't strip in provider:model strings)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

`agent/model_metadata.py` keeps a hand-maintained frozenset, `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES`, that `_strip_provider_prefix()` uses to recognise `provider:model` strings before metadata and context-window lookups. Providers that ship as plugins are not in it, so a string like `fireworks:accounts/fireworks/models/foo` (or any user plugin under `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/model-providers/`, e.g. `alibaba-token-plan:qwen3.7-plus`) never strips. The full string then misses cache and models.dev lookups and falls back to default context lengths.

The same file already solves this exact problem for URL reverse-mapping: `_URL_TO_PROVIDER` auto-extends from registered provider profiles right below its static dict. The prefix set just never got the same treatment, so every new provider plugin silently needs a core edit to be recognised in `provider:model` strings, which is the kind of core edit the plugin surface is meant to avoid.

### Proposed Solution

Auto-extend `_PROVIDER_PREFIXES` from registered profiles, mirroring the `_URL_TO_PROVIDER` block: after discovery, add each profile's `name` and `aliases` (lowercased) to the set. The existing `_OLLAMA_TAG_PATTERN` guard already prevents over-stripping of Ollama `model:tag` strings, so behaviour for those is unchanged.

I have this implemented with a test and will open a PR referencing this issue.

### Alternatives Considered

Keep hand-adding names to the frozenset per provider. That is what happens today (#7575 was this same gap for xAI and was fixed by adding `xai`, `grok` and friends by hand), it works for bundled plugins (though several, like `fireworks`, are currently missing) but cannot work for user plugins, which by design never touch this file.

### Feature Type

Developer experience / plugin surface

### Scope

Small. One auto-extend block in `agent/model_metadata.py` plus a test in `tests/agent/test_model_metadata.py`. No behaviour change for anything already in the static set.

items.title: bug(update): pre-update snapshot covers only invoking profile while all gateways restart

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug description

`hermes update` creates its pre-update quick snapshot only for the profile that invoked the update, but later restarts every running profile gateway because the code checkout is shared.

This leaves non-invoking profiles exposed to configuration or migration regressions without a contemporaneous rollback point.

## Source-level cause

`_run_pre_update_backup()` calls `create_quick_snapshot(...)` without an explicit `hermes_home`, so `create_quick_snapshot()` resolves only the active profile through `get_hermes_home()`.

Later in the same update flow, `main.py` explicitly performs:

> Auto-restart ALL gateways after update.

The backup scope and restart scope therefore do not match.

## Reproduction

1. Configure and run gateways for two named profiles, `profile-a` and `profile-b`.
2. Give each profile a distinct `config.yaml`.
3. Run `hermes --profile profile-a update` (or invoke `/update` through profile A).
4. Observe that all running gateways are restarted.
5. Inspect `state-snapshots/`:
   - profile A has the new `pre-update` snapshot;
   - profile B has no snapshot from that update.

## Observed impact

In a real multi-profile installation, an update initiated under one profile restarted another profile after several previously customized values had reverted to defaults. The non-invoking profile had no same-update snapshot; its newest usable snapshot was several days old. A full restore from that older snapshot would also have reverted later intentional settings.

No credentials, channel identifiers, or private configuration values are included in this report.

## Expected behavior

Before mutating shared code or restarting gateways, the updater should create and verify a separate pre-update snapshot for every profile whose gateway it will restart.

At minimum:

- enumerate the default profile and all running named-profile gateways;
- create a profile-local quick snapshot for each affected profile;
- report the profile-to-snapshot mapping;
- ensure the snapshot includes `config.yaml`;
- keep restore and post-update safety checks profile-scoped;
- add regression coverage for “update from profile A while profile B is running.”

## Suggested implementation direction

Make `_run_pre_update_backup()` return a profile-to-snapshot mapping rather than a single active-profile snapshot ID. Reuse the same affected-profile discovery used by the all-gateway restart path, then pass each profile home explicitly to `create_quick_snapshot(hermes_home=...)`.

The existing active-profile cron restore safety net can continue using the invoking profile’s snapshot while follow-up work can extend post-update validation per profile.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: git installation, v0.18.2-era main
- Host: Linux with systemd user services
- Multiple named profiles with simultaneously running gateways

items.title: [Bug]: Installer-created .install_method dirties Git checkouts

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Bug Description

The Git-based installer writes `.install_method` into the Hermes Agent
checkout, but the file is not ignored by Git.

This leaves a managed installation with a dirty working tree. Because
`hermes update` detects changes using `git status --porcelain` and stashes
untracked files with `git stash push --include-untracked`, this runtime marker
can trigger unnecessary stash and restore operations during updates.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install or update Hermes using the Git-based installation method.

2. Enter the managed checkout:

   ```shell
   cd ~/src/hermes-agent
   ```

3. Check the working tree:

   ```shell
   git status --short
   git check-ignore -v .install_method
   ```

4. Observe that `.install_method` is untracked and has no matching ignore rule.

### Expected Behavior

The installer-created runtime marker should be ignored by Git. It should not
dirty the checkout or trigger the updater's local-change handling.

### Actual Behavior

`.install_method` appears as an untracked file:

```text
?? .install_method
```

Running `git check-ignore -v .install_method` produces no output, confirming
that the file has no matching ignore rule.

### Affected Component

Installer / updater

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A — not gateway-related

### Debug Report

Not applicable — this is a deterministic Git-ignore issue involving an
installer-generated runtime file.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

### Python Version

3.12.3

### Hermes Version

0.18.2

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

None.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`scripts/install.sh` writes `.install_method` into the installation tree, and
`hermes_cli/config.py` reads it as runtime installation metadata.

However, the repository's root `.gitignore` does not ignore this file. The
updater detects local changes using `git status --porcelain` and stashes
untracked files with `git stash push --include-untracked`, so the
installer-generated marker is treated as a local modification.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add the root-scoped installer marker to `.gitignore`:

```gitignore
# Installation method marker generated by the installer
/.install_method
```

Root-scoping the rule avoids ignoring similarly named files in nested
directories.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

## Feature Request

### Problem
Hermes Desktop (Electron app) has no system tray support. Closing the window quits the app entirely, and minimizing only goes to the Windows taskbar. For an always-on AI agent that runs background tasks, cron jobs, and long-running operations, this is a significant usability gap.

### Current Behavior
- `new Tray` is not used anywhere in the app (verified in app.asar)
- No `contextMenu`, no `setContextMenu`, no `isQuitting` flag
- Closing the window = app exits, killing all background work
- Minimizing goes to taskbar, not tray

### Proposed Solution
Add system tray support:
1. **Tray icon** with the Hermes logo in the system notification area
2. **Minimize to tray** - clicking minimize sends the app to the tray instead of the taskbar
3. **Close to tray** - clicking the X hides the window to the tray; the app keeps running in the background (with a "Quit" option in the tray context menu)
4. **Tray context menu** with options: Show/Hide window, Quit
5. **Unread badge** on the tray icon when there are new messages or task completions (optional, nice-to-have)

### Why
Hermes Agent is designed to run background tasks (cron jobs, delegated tasks, gateway sessions). Users need the desktop app to stay alive without occupying taskbar space. Every major Electron app (Discord, Slack, VS Code) implements this pattern.

### Environment
- Hermes Desktop v0.18.0 (official Electron app)
- Windows 10
- Hermes Agent v0.18.2

### Problem or Use Case

Hermes Agent stores all data in hardcoded SQLite files. This is a fundamental security limitation that cannot be worked around at the application level.

For a personal AI system that accumulates years of private conversations, sensitive knowledge, health information, political views, financial discussions, and everything else a person talks to their AI about - plaintext files on disk are problematic and unmanageable.

### Proposed Solution

**What a pluggable backend solves**

- **Encryption at rest:** Column-level or tablespace encryption via pgcrypto, TDE, or native database encryption
- **Data compartmentalization:** Under compelled access, database credentials can be separate from system access
- **Separate authentication:** Database credentials independent of filesystem access
- **Row-level security:** PostgreSQL RLS for fine-grained access control over different data categories
- **Centralized security management:** Same security policies, same backup/encryption strategy, same audit trail as the rest of the AI ecosystem

items.title: Desktop: composer model selection overridden by session.info gateway event on every poll
items.body:
Description

    In the desktop app, selecting a different model from the composer model dropdown works momentarily, but the
    selection is silently reverted within 1-3 seconds. The user cannot change the model through the UI — it always
    jumps back to the backend profile default (or whatever the backend last broadcast via session.info).

    Steps to Reproduce

    1. Open Hermes Desktop app
    2. Locate the model dropdown in the composer area
    3. Click to select a model different from the current one (e.g. switch from deepseek-chat to deepseek-v4-flash)
    4. Observe the dropdown reverts to the previous model within seconds
    5. Check DevTools console for [MODEL_DEBUG] logs

    Actual Behavior

    The model selection is overridden. Console logs show three distinct writes to setCurrentModel:


    [MODEL_DEBUG] setCurrentModel: "deepseek-v4-flash"     <- user click
    [MODEL_DEBUG] setCurrentModel: "deepseek-chat"          <- handleGatewayEvent via session.info (overwrites)
    [MODEL_DEBUG] setCurrentModel: "deepseek-chat"          <- syncRuntimeMetadataToView (duplicate)


    The second write originates from handleGatewayEvent processing the session.info event, which overwrites the
    localStorage value the user just set.

    Expected Behavior

    Selecting a model from the composer dropdown should persist until the user manually changes it again. The gateway
    event should not overwrite the user's explicit selection.

    Root Cause

    In apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts, the session.info event handler
    unconditionally calls setCurrentModel and setCurrentProvider inside the if (apply) block:

    typescript
    if (apply) {
      if (modelChanged) {
        setCurrentModel(payload!.model || '')
      }
      if (providerChanged) {
        setCurrentProvider(payload!.provider || '')
      }
      // ... cwd, branch, personality, etc.
    }


    Two problems:
    1. When there is no active session (apply = !activeSessionIdRef.current): the backend broadcasts
    session.info with model.default from config.yaml, which overwrites the user's sticky choice stored in
    localStorage via the composer.
    2. When there is an active session: session-state-cache::syncRuntimeMetadataToView already syncs
    model/provider from the session state — the session.info write here is redundant and races against it.

    Suggested Fix

    Remove the setCurrentModel and setCurrentProvider calls from the if (apply) block in the session.info
    event handler. The composer's model state should only be managed by:
    - User selection in the dropdown (persisted to localStorage)
    - syncRuntimeMetadataToView (from session state cache)

    The other fields (cwd, branch, personality, reasoning_effort, service_tier, fast, yolo) are safe to
    keep as-is.

    Affected File
    - apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts

    Reference
    A local fix was applied and verified:
    - npx tsc --noEmit -> zero errors
    - npx vite build -> successful
    - node scripts/bundle-electron-main.mjs -> successful
    - npx electron-builder --dir -> successful

    Environment

    - OS: Windows 10
    - Hermes Desktop (release/win-unpacked build)
    - CLI version is NOT affected (the issue is unique to the desktop UI composer)

items.title: [Bug]: Multimodal content list crashes interim processing and retries until API-call budget is exhausted

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug description

After an image/vision turn or context compaction, a follow-up turn can enter an effectively infinite retry loop and eventually fail with:

```text
I apologize, but I encountered repeated errors:
Error during OpenAI-compatible API call #59: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'list'
```

This was reproduced in a real Telegram gateway session. The provider requests themselves completed successfully; the failure happened afterward while Hermes processed the previous assistant message.

## Actual traceback

```text
agent/conversation_loop.py:4874 in run_conversation
    agent._interim_assistant_visible_text(previous_msg)
run_agent.py:4824 in _interim_assistant_visible_text
    return self._strip_think_blocks(content or "").strip()
agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:678 in strip_think_blocks
    content = re.sub(r'<think>.*?</think>', '', content, ...)
TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'list'
```

The same traceback repeated on every outer-loop retry, including API calls #55, #56, #57, #58, and #59.

## Root cause

`assistant_msg["content"]` is not guaranteed to be a string. After multimodal/image turns or compaction it may be a typed content-parts list, for example:

```python
[
    {"type": "text", "text": "..."},
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "..."}},
]
```

`AIAgent._interim_assistant_visible_text()` passes this list directly to `_strip_think_blocks()`, which ultimately calls `re.sub()` and raises. Because the previous message remains unchanged, every retry deterministically fails at the same point.

The hardcoded wording `Error during OpenAI-compatible API call` is also misleading here: the failure is local post-response processing, not an OpenAI-compatible endpoint failure.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Hermes through the Telegram gateway with a model/provider using structured content.
2. Send an image, or otherwise create a multimodal content-parts message; context compaction may also produce the shape.
3. Send a follow-up request that causes tool calls/interim assistant handling.
4. Observe repeated `expected string or bytes-like object, got 'list'` failures until the API-call budget is exhausted.

## Expected behavior

- Interim-visible-text extraction should normalize typed content parts to plain text before regex processing.
- Image-only/non-text content should safely produce an empty string or marker.
- One local post-processing exception should not cause dozens of identical provider retries.
- Error text should identify the actual local processing stage/provider rather than always saying `OpenAI-compatible API call`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Current upstream observed at `bd208a6d7`
- Python 3.11.14
- OpenAI SDK 2.24.0
- Telegram gateway
- Provider: OpenAI Codex (`gpt-5.6-sol`)

## Related fixes already proposed

Two open PRs address this exact crash but there was no standalone tracking issue found:

- #66235 — narrow normalization in `_interim_assistant_visible_text`
- #66218 — broader coercion in the shared think-block stripping helper

This issue is intended to track the user-visible regression and its retry-loop impact, and to give both PRs a shared bug reference.

items.title: [Bug]:  Tirith circuit breaker ignores fail_open: false — security guard silently fails open
items.body:
### Bug Description

When the Tirith circuit breaker opens (after 3 consecutive spawn failures), the guard returns allow unconditionally, ignoring the operator's configured `fail_open: false`. Tirith is then disabled for the remainder of the process, silently.

An operator who explicitly configured fail-closed gets fail-open behaviour. Nothing surfaces to the user — only a log line. The guard appears configured and enabled; it is neither.

Three properties make this worse than a plain fail-open default:
1. It overrides an explicit operator choice, rather than being a default.
2. It is sticky — once open, the guard stays disabled for the rest of the process, not just for the failing call.
3. It is reachable by anything that can cause three failures: a transient environment problem, a binary missing or renamed after an upgrade, resource exhaustion.

We found it only through positive-control testing. Configuration alone gave no signal that the guard had stopped evaluating.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Tirith with `fail_open: false`.
2. Cause three consecutive spawn failures (e.g. point the Tirith binary path at a non-existent file).
3. Observe the log line: `tirith circuit breaker opened after 3 consecutive failures; disabling for the rest of the process`.
4. Issue any command Tirith would normally block — e.g. a plain-HTTP download:
   `curl http://example.com/x -o /tmp/x`

### Expected Behavior

The command is denied. `fail_open: false` means fail-closed: if the guard cannot evaluate, deny.

Control tests confirm the setting works correctly OUTSIDE the breaker path:
- Tirith broken + fail_open: false  -> approved=False ("tirith spawn failed (fail-closed)")  [correct]
- Tirith broken + fail_open: true   -> approved=True                                          [correct for that setting]

### Actual Behavior

The command is approved. With the breaker open, allow is returned without consulting `fail_open`:
- Breaker open + fail_open: false  -> approved=True   [the bug]
- Breaker open + fail_open: true   -> approved=True   [correct for that setting]

### Affected Component

Other, Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
report
```

### Operating System

Fedora 44

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream 311a5b0a · local c86f9613

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`tools/tirith_security.py`, breaker-open path (~line 753): the function returns an allow result without consulting the configured `fail_open`.

The upstream rationale for the breaker is avoiding a retry loop on repeated spawn failures — a rationale that assumes fail-open semantics. When the operator has set `fail_open: false`, "allow everything" inverts the requested behaviour and defeats the exact setting meant to prevent it.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Honour `fail_open` in the breaker-open path:
- fail_open: true  -> keep current behaviour (allow; preserves the intent of avoiding a retry loop)
- fail_open: false -> deny while the breaker is open

This still avoids the retry loop — the breaker's actual purpose — because the decision is returned without re-spawning Tirith.

We run exactly this as a local patch. Verified: breaker open + fail_open:false -> block; breaker open + fail_open:true -> allow.

Additionally: consider surfacing breaker-open as a visible warning to the operator, not only a log line. Any state where a configured security control stops evaluating deserves to be loud.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

## Standardize local imports to the `src.` path

### Background
The repo root **and** `src/` are both on `sys.path`, so in a live process `import x` and `import src.x` resolve to **two separate module objects** with separate classes and module-level state. This splits the API/engine boundary: `isinstance(engine_obj, src.items.Item)` returns `False`, and module-level registries (e.g. `items.unique_items_spawned`, the `narration` context buffer) can desync. Two regressions traced to this: the narration/chest-contents fallback (fixed in `2ba8fa5`) and the broader boundary split.

**Mitigated at runtime** by `src/import_sync.py` (commit `a890fb2`), which aliases bare<->src at the entry points so the running process uses one object per module. This issue tracks the **proper fix**: convert every bare local import to the canonical `src.` path so the sync hook *and* the `try/except ImportError` + `type(x).__name__ ==` scar tissue in `src/api/` can eventually be removed.

items.title: Photon iMessage voice notes bypass STT pipeline and interrupt active tasks

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug

iMessage voice notes received through the Photon adapter are **never auto-transcribed** by the STT pipeline. Instead, a U+FFFC placeholder character arrives as a text message, which:

1. Triggers a spurious agent turn ("⚡ Interrupting current task..."), disrupting any active conversation
2. Produces no transcription — the agent receives an empty text message instead of the voice content

The actual audio file (`.caf`) may arrive separately as an attachment, but it is classified as `MessageType.DOCUMENT` or `MessageType.AUDIO`, bypassing the STT routing logic entirely (the gateway only transcribes `MessageType.VOICE`).

## Root cause

The `@spectrum-ts/imessage` SDK (cloud gRPC mode, used by the Photon sidecar) has three issues:

### 1. Voice notes classified as `attachment`, not `voice`
The SDK classifies all inbound attachments as `type: "attachment"` — it never calls `asVoice()` on the inbound path. The `isAudioMessage` protobuf flag (tag 320) is ignored by the inbound mapper.

### 2. U+FFFC placeholder fires before CloudKit syncs the attachment
Apple's gRPC cloud push emits a U+FFFC text placeholder where the attachment should be, but `attachments` is still empty. The local SDK path has a retry (`refetchUntilAttachmentsSettle`), but the remote/cloud path has none.

### 3. CAF format not supported by cloud STT providers
The `.caf` file cannot be parsed by cloud Whisper APIs. Additionally, `audio/x-caf` was mapped to `.mp3` extension, producing corrupt files.

## Expected behavior

When a user sends an iMessage voice note via Photon:

1. The U+FFFC placeholder should **not** trigger a spurious agent turn or interrupt the active task
2. The real audio attachment should be detected and classified as `MessageType.VOICE`
3. The audio should be converted from CAF to WAV (using ffmpeg or afconvert)
4. The WAV file should be sent to the configured STT provider (e.g., Groq Whisper)
5. The transcription should be delivered to the agent as the message text
6. If no attachment arrives within a reasonable timeout, a warning should be logged

## Environment

- Hermes Agent with Photon adapter (spectrum-ts cloud gRPC mode)
- STT provider: Groq Whisper (`whisper-large-v3`)
- Platform: macOS

## Related

- #38299 (Feishu): same class of bug — voice messages routed as AUDIO instead of VOICE
- #57882 (LINE): same class of bug — audio routed through image cache instead of STT
- #54514 (Photon): fixes a media placeholder race condition but does not address STT

## Workaround

A PR with fixes is available at https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/66326, containing commits that:
1. Map `audio/x-caf` to `.caf` extension (was `.mp3`)
2. Promote `.caf` attachments to `MessageType.VOICE`
3. Handle U+FFFC placeholder with a non-blocking deferred wait (15s timeout)
4. Add `.caf` to `SUPPORTED_FORMATS` + CAF→WAV conversion via ffmpeg/afconvert
