items.title: [Bug]: Desktop won't open — failed self-update leaves hermes-setup alive, live update marker blocks boot forever ("An update is finishing…" loop)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

A failed self-update can leave the staged updater (`~/.hermes/hermes-setup --update`) **running forever after it has already logged `state=Failed`**. Because the process never exits, the `~/.hermes/.hermes-update-in-progress` marker it wrote at startup stays "live" (its recorded pid is alive), and the desktop boot gate (`readLiveUpdateMarker()` in `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`) defers backend start on every launch, looping the boot screen line:

```
[boot] An update is finishing — Hermes will start automatically when it completes…
```

To the user this presents as **"the desktop app won't open at all"** — clicking `/Applications/Hermes.app` again just logs `hermes already installed — relaunched desktop; exiting installer` and the fresh instance blocks on the same marker. The marker's staleness self-heal only fires when the recorded pid is dead, so a failed-but-alive updater defeats it indefinitely.

Observed and recovered on a live install today; full evidence below.

## Timeline (live install, macOS 26.3 arm64, hermes 0.18.2)

1. `22:04` — auto-update starts: `~/.hermes/hermes-setup --update --branch main --target-app ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app` (pid 8155). Writes `~/.hermes/.hermes-update-in-progress` (line 1 = `8155`, line 2 = unix ts).
2. GitHub was unreachable from this network at the time. `bootstrap-installer.log`:
   ```
   ✗ Network error — cannot reach the remote repository.
     fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git/': Error in the HTTP2 framing layer
   [update] first update attempt failed; retrying once …
   ✗ Network error — cannot reach the remote repository.
     fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git/': Failed to connect to github.com port 443 after 75008 ms: Couldn't connect to server
   INFO hermes_bootstrap_lib::update: update stage stage=update state=Failed duration_ms=Some(172966) error=Some("hermes update failed (exit Some(1)). See .../update.log for details.")
   ```
   So by `22:07:40` the update had **terminally failed**.
3. `22:12` — user clicks `/Applications/Hermes.app` four times; each run logs `hermes already installed — relaunched desktop; exiting installer`.
4. Desktop instances start but never leave the boot screen; `desktop.log` fills with one `An update is finishing — Hermes will start automatically when it completes…` line per second (`UPDATE_WAIT_POLL_MS = 1000`, bounded by `UPDATE_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 20 min` — but a relaunch restarts the wait, and users give up long before 20 minutes).
5. `22:18` — 14 minutes after the update failed, the updater process was still there:
   ```
   PID  PPID STAT STARTED                      ELAPSED COMMAND
   8155    1 Ss   五 7月/17 22:04:45 2026      13:50   ~/.hermes/hermes-setup --update --branch main --target-app …
   ```
   with one unreaped zombie child:
   ```
   8293  8155 <defunct>
   ```
   and no open sockets (`lsof -p 8155 -a -i` → empty). It was not doing anything — it had simply failed without exiting.

## Root cause (two bugs stacked)

1. **`hermes-setup` fail-without-exit.** After the update stage records `state=Failed`, the process keeps running (the `<defunct>` child suggests a missing `wait()`/exit path after the failed retry). `UpdateMarkerGuard` removes the marker on updater exit — which never happens.
2. **The boot gate's staleness check trusts pid liveness alone.** `readLiveUpdateMarker()` treats "marker pid alive" as "update in progress". A wedged updater is indistinguishable from a healthy one, even though `bootstrap-installer.log` already contains a `state=Failed` entry *newer than the marker timestamp*.

The network outage is only the trigger; any deterministic update failure that hits this code path would wedge the same way.

## Verified workaround

```bash
kill <pid from line 1 of ~/.hermes/.hermes-update-in-progress>
rm ~/.hermes/.hermes-update-in-progress
open ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app
```

App then boots normally (`HERMES_BACKEND_READY` → `Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup`).

## Suggested fixes

- **(a)** `hermes-setup` must exit (non-zero) once the update stage reaches `state=Failed` after its retry, reaping children, so `UpdateMarkerGuard` clears the marker.
- **(b)** Defense in depth in the desktop boot gate: treat the marker as stale when the updater's own log records a terminal `state=Failed` newer than the marker timestamp (or give the marker a TTL refreshed by updater heartbeat), instead of pid-liveness alone.
- **(c)** UX: after N minutes on the update-wait boot screen, offer a "skip waiting / cancel update" affordance instead of a silent 20-minute spinner.

## Related

- #64577 — four other failure modes of the same macOS self-update stack (stale staged updater, silent backup, canonical-app desync, retryable-error UX). This report is a fifth, distinct mode: fail-without-exit + live marker blocking boot. Its "Cause 2" note that cancelling voids the marker's mutual exclusion is the mirror image of this bug (here the marker is *over*-honored).
- #50238 — introduced the update-in-progress marker.
- #57645 — macOS in-app update closes without updating (different mode: there the updater dies too early; here it never dies).

## Environment

- macOS 26.3 (arm64), install root `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`, hermes 0.18.2
- Staged updater `~/.hermes/hermes-setup` signed 2026-06-06 (`com.nousresearch.hermes.setup`)
- Evidence available on request: `desktop.log`, `bootstrap-installer.log`, `ps` captures, marker file contents

items.title: Telegram polling reconnect ladder stalls mid-way — gateway alive but silently dead, Restart=always never fires

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Summary

The Telegram gateway becomes silently and permanently unresponsive: the
`hermes-gateway` process stays `active (running)` for hours while consuming zero
Telegram updates. Because the process never exits, `Restart=always` never fires and
there is no self-recovery — only a manual `systemctl restart hermes-gateway` restores
the bot.

**Component:** `gateway/platforms/telegram.py` — `_handle_polling_network_error` /
`_verify_polling_after_reconnect`
**Severity:** High (messaging gateway silently dead; no automatic recovery)

### Environment

- hermes-agent **0.17.0** (editable install, commit `2bd1977`)
- Single-platform deployment (Telegram only), systemd-managed with `Restart=always`
- Flaky egress link between the host and `api.telegram.org` (≈39 `TimedOut` blips over 3 days)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the gateway against Telegram over a link that intermittently produces
   `telegram.error.TimedOut` on the long-poll connection.
2. Wait for a `TimedOut` to land mid-reconnect-ladder (below the
   `MAX_NETWORK_RETRIES` escalation threshold).
3. Observe the ladder log "reconnecting in Ns" and then go silent.

### Actual behavior

The reconnect ladder in `_handle_polling_network_error` (telegram.py ~L1439–1512)
**stalls mid-ladder** instead of advancing to the fatal-restart escalation.

Observed journal (UTC):

    21:33:18  telegram.error.TimedOut: Timed out
    21:33:18  [Telegram] Telegram polling reconnect failed: Timed out
    21:33:18  [Telegram] Telegram network error (attempt 4/10), reconnecting in 40s. Error: Timed out
    <silence for ~2 hours until a manual restart>

The ladder reached **attempt 4/10**, logged "reconnecting in 40s," and never advanced
to attempt 5. It never reached the `attempt > MAX_NETWORK_RETRIES` branch (L1457) that
calls `_set_fatal_error(..., retryable=True)`, so the platform was never queued for
background reconnection and never escalated.

The code documents the exact state it defends against (L1491–1504): after
`start_polling()` returns, PTB's `Updater` can be left with `running == True` while the
underlying long-poll task is wedged on a stale httpx connection and makes no progress;
no `error_callback` fires, so the ladder won't advance on its own. The mitigation —
`_verify_polling_after_reconnect` (L1515+), a deferred probe that sleeps
`HEARTBEAT_PROBE_DELAY` (60s), checks `Updater.running`, then probes the bot endpoint
with a tight timeout and re-enters the ladder on failure — did **not** recover the
connection in this incident (ladder frozen at attempt 4 for ~2h). Likely one of: the
probe was not scheduled, the probe coroutine itself wedged (endpoint probe hung despite
the intended timeout), or an exception in the probe/re-entry path was swallowed without
escalating.

### Why `Restart=always` does not help

By design: `run.py:_handle_adapter_fatal_error` (~L3346–3400) handles a retryable
adapter failure by **keeping the process alive** and queuing the platform for
background reconnection (`_failed_platforms`), exiting for a service restart only when
no adapters and no queued platforms remain. So even on a *successful* escalation the
process stays up and relies on the in-process reconnect watcher. When the ladder stalls
*before* escalating (as here), the platform is never queued — the gateway is alive with
a dead Telegram adapter that nothing is retrying.

### Expected behavior

The reconnect ladder always makes progress: it either advances the attempt counter or
escalates. A stalled or swallowed probe must not leave the ladder frozen, and a
single-platform gateway should ultimately reach a state an external supervisor can
recover.

### Suggested fix directions

1. **Guarantee ladder progress.** Ensure `_handle_polling_network_error` always
   advances the attempt counter or escalates. Add a monotonic watchdog independent of
   the probe: if no successful `getUpdates` cycle has completed within N seconds,
   force-escalate regardless of `Updater.running`.
2. **Harden `_verify_polling_after_reconnect`.** Make the endpoint probe's timeout
   authoritative (a wedged httpx pool must not hang the probe itself) and ensure any
   probe exception re-enters the ladder rather than terminating the recovery task
   silently.
3. **Optional process-exit on unrecoverable single-platform failure.** For
   single-platform deployments, "keep alive with a dead adapter and rely on background
   reconnection" degrades to "silently dead" if the watcher stalls. An option to
   exit-for-service-restart when the sole platform is unrecoverable would let systemd
   guarantee recovery.

### Workaround in place (no upstream change required)

An external liveness monitor watches the **outcome** rather than internal state: it
polls Telegram `getWebhookInfo.pending_update_count` on a timer and restarts the
gateway after N consecutive non-zero readings (gateway not consuming updates). It is
version-agnostic and survives the in-process stall because it never depends on the
ladder advancing. The detection window is bounded below by `agent.gateway_timeout`, so
a legitimate long turn (which also pauses update consumption) self-aborts before the
monitor acts and is never false-restarted. This is a safety net, not a fix — guaranteed
recovery belongs in the reconnect ladder itself.

items.body:
### Bug Description

When the dashboard runs with `--open-profile <name>`, changing the model via the dashboard writes `model.default` / `model.provider` into the **default profile's** `~/.hermes/config.yaml` instead of `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/config.yaml`. The UI reports success, the gateway for the open profile keeps running the old model, and there is no error anywhere. From the user's perspective the model switch silently never happens.

This is another instance of the HERMES_HOME propagation gap discussed in #18594 (closed): the dashboard's subprocess spawner does not pass `HERMES_HOME` for the open profile, so the config writer falls back to the default home. The runtime even warns about it:

```
[HERMES_HOME fallback] HERMES_HOME is unset but active profile is 'trading-agent'. Falling back to /Users/user/.hermes, which is the DEFAULT profile - not 'trading-agent'. Any data this process writes will land in the wrong profile. The subprocess spawner should pass HERMES_HOME explicitly (see issue #18594).
```

Related wrong-profile family: #41422, #65828, #46408.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `hermes -p default dashboard --port 9119 --open-profile trading-agent` (launchd), plus a separate `hermes --profile trading-agent gateway run` process
2. In the dashboard (profile `trading-agent` open), switch the model, e.g. to `gpt-5.6-sol`
3. Inspect configs

### Expected Behavior

`~/.hermes/profiles/trading-agent/config.yaml` gets `model.default: gpt-5.6-sol`

### Actual Behavior

`~/.hermes/config.yaml` (default profile) gets `model.default: gpt-5.6-sol`; the trading-agent profile keeps its previous model. No error shown.

### Affected Component

Dashboard / profile subprocess spawning

### Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), macOS 15.7.1, profiles via launchd with per-profile `HERMES_HOME`

### Workaround

Edit `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/config.yaml` directly and restart that profile's gateway.

items.body:
# [Feature tracker] Boardstate — the board your agent builds with you

> **The board your agent builds with you — durable, auditable, operator-governed.**

Hermes' agent can already *do* almost anything. What it can't do today is leave you a
**place**: a persistent, visual workspace it composes, updates, and operates — that you
co-own, audit, and govern. This tracker covers the Boardstate delivery: the bundling PR
(#66381), what's inside it, how to test every claim in one checkout, and the roadmap.

![The agent builds the board, one-click live templates, and an operator-governed OfficeCLI action — one unedited take](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/boardstate-hermes-plugin/main/.github/media/hero.gif)

Agent-buildable dashboards are becoming table stakes — Codex- and Anthropic-class
tooling (Conway) now generate no-code dashboards into sandboxes. Those are throwaway:
un-audited, outside the product, gone with the sandbox. Boardstate is that capability
**inside Hermes**, built on one idea: **the board is a validated document** — one
writer, every mutation through gated verbs, so agents and humans literally cannot
diverge. Durable where theirs are disposable; governed where theirs are unaccountable.

## Architecture (two diagrams)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Clients
    B[Web dashboard tab]
    D[Desktop app page]
    A[Hermes agent]
  end
  subgraph Backend["plugin_api.py (dashboard process)"]
    WS[WS bridge - session gate]
    MCP[MCP proxy - nonce]
    OP["/operator - session + allowlist + operator secret"]
    AS[tokenized asset route - capability token]
  end
  subgraph Sidecar["Node sidecar (loopback, per-spawn nonce)"]
    H[single host - one writer]
    ST[(workspace.json)]
    BR[connector broker]
  end
  EXT[External MCP tools - OfficeCLI, ...]
  B --> WS --> H
  D --> WS
  A --> MCP --> H
  B -.approve/confirm.-> OP --> H
  B --> AS --> H
  H --> ST
  H --> BR --> EXT
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Agent
  participant Board as Board (single host)
  participant Operator
  Agent->>Board: tool_search / request grant
  Board->>Operator: approvals widget: REQUESTED
  Operator->>Board: approve (gated route, per-tool)
  Agent->>Board: invoke mutating tool
  Board->>Operator: action PARKS (bounded TTL)
  Operator->>Board: confirm
  Board->>Agent: result (redacted errors, hash-gated)
```

## The capability ladder (the mental model)

1. **Trusted builtins** — 16 widget kinds rendered by the host: stat-card, chart
   (line/bar/area/sparkline/gauge), table, markdown, notes, activity, action-form,
   action-button, chat, sessions, usage, cron, instances, agent-status, approvals,
   preview/iframe-embed.
2. **Sandboxed custom widgets** — agent- or gallery-authored HTML widgets in an
   opaque-origin iframe, no-network CSP, capability manifest, **approval-gated mount**
   (pending assets uniformly 404). Games, calculators, trackers — running *inside*
   Hermes, jailed:

   ![The library's 2048 installed, approved, and played inside Hermes — sandboxed, no network](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/boardstate-hermes-plugin/main/.github/media/game-2048.gif)

3. **Governed connectors** — external MCP tools behind operator grants: the agent
   *requests*, you approve per-tool; reads pass a manifest-hash gate (a connector that
   changes its tools re-pends for re-approval); **mutations always park for your
   confirm** (bounded — never hangs). OfficeCLI preset included.

## What's in the box (feature map)

| Tier | Surface | Details |
|------|---------|---------|
| Foundation | Live board, one writer | `<boardstate-view>` over an authed WS bridge; single sidecar per state dir (port-file adoption); export/import, undo, history |
| Data | Live Hermes bindings | usage / sessions / instances / cron self-bind to the dashboard's own REST; allowlisted rpc bindings for stat-cards/charts/tables; never an error cell |
| Agent | 19 MCP tools | workspace/tab/widget CRUD, scaffold, catalog, data_read, design_review, board_view, tool_search, undo — every write lands live |
| Design | Native both surfaces | theme tokens follow live palette swaps ([swap take](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/boardstate-hermes-plugin/main/.github/media/theme-swap.gif)); web speaks the dashboard's design language, desktop the macOS one |
| Templates | One-click live boards | Agent HQ · Usage & Cost · Sessions Monitor · Office Ops (grants + actions self-contained) |
| Operational | Connector broker | grants lifecycle, pending-action engine, OfficeCLI preset, per-tool approval, redacted errors, anti-rug-pull |
| i18n | 20 locales | ar de es fa fr hi id it ja ko nl pl pt-BR ru th tr uk vi zh-CN zh-TW (library strings) |
| Desktop | Phase 2 | the same backend already powers a real Electron page — **PR #66425** (issue #66415) |

## Try every claim (one checkout)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/100yenadmin/boardstate-hermes-plugin && cd boardstate-hermes-plugin
npm ci && npm run build          # 23 node suites + 3 python in CI; run any locally:
node test/operational-e2e.mjs    # request → approve → invoke → park → confirm → result
node test/custom-widget.mjs      # pending 404s; approved serves with the CSP jail
node test/rugpull-repend.mjs     # manifest drift re-pends the grant, never executes
node test/secret-redaction.mjs   # connector config never reaches the agent surface
# install into a dashboard:
mkdir -p ~/.hermes/plugins/boardstate && cp -r dashboard ~/.hermes/plugins/boardstate/
# + enable `boardstate` under plugins.enabled, restart `hermes dashboard`
```

| Do this | Observe |
|---------|---------|
| Open the **Board** tab | renders in the active theme; follows a palette swap live |
| Ask the agent for a stat card | it appears live, no reload |
| Click **Agent HQ** | live usage/sessions/instances/cron, zero error cells |
| Author `boardstate.connectors.json`, restart | approvals widget shows the **requested** grant |
| Approve the tool, click the Office Ops action | it **parks**; confirm; a real `.docx` lands |
| Install + approve a widget bundle (e.g. the library's `twenty48`) | pending assets 404; after approve it mounts sandboxed and is playable |
| Kill Node / uninstall | dashboard unaffected; the tab degrades to a clear message |

## The receipts (what users have asked for)

- #56808 — *Dashboard Design*: a composable, owner-editable dashboard surface.
- #15614 / #15182 — *Spotify dashboard widgets*: the general answer is a governed
  custom-widget platform, not one-off widgets.
- #34566 — *UI branding / visual identity*: the board adopts the host design language
  (numerically matched), not its own.
- #66138 — *dashboard i18n*: the library ships 20 locales.

## Scale, honestly

| | LOC |
|---|---|
| Library (`@boardstate/*` on npm, MIT) — source | ~29,600 |
| Library incl. tests (901 cases + 16-case conformance suite) | 45,772 |
| Hermes plugin (source + 23 node suites + 3 python) | ~5,200 |

The bundled PR ships the plugin + built artifacts (kanban precedent); the library rides
as vendored bundles. Raw diff ≫ reviewable source — the reviewable plugin surface is
~5k lines.

**Security posture:** hardened through three independent adversarial review passes plus
a full external review round before submission — including two real holes those passes
caught and fixed with revert-checked regressions (secret redaction on every
agent-facing error; the manifest-hash gate on every agent-reachable connector call).
Operator verbs ride a dedicated non-persisted secret; the sandbox CSP survives the
asset proxy verbatim.

## Roadmap

| Item | Where |
|------|-------|
| Web dashboard plugin (bundled) | **PR #66381** (this tracker's subject) |
| Desktop app page (real-Electron proven) | **PR #66425** (stacked on #66381; issue #66415) |
| Widget gallery hosting + more bundles | plugin repo roadmap |
| Aggregator connector recipes (remote MCP) | plugin repo roadmap |
| In-board chat widget | plugin repo roadmap |

## What this deliberately is NOT

- Not a core change: one directory on the existing dashboard-plugin contract; no new
  Python deps; graceful without Node.
- Not a third-party product integration: MIT, self-contained, zero external services —
  it integrates Hermes with itself, like kanban.
- Not a fork-and-forget: canonical source + CI live in the plugin repo; we maintain it
  and sync releases — or Hermes absorbs and owns it (adoption-model section in the PR).

items.title: [Bug]: mcp_stdio_watchdog breaks uvx-based MCP servers — "Connection closed" after handshake

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

Stdio MCP servers launched via `uvx` fail to connect when run through the gateway. The connection fails with "Connection closed" after 3 retry attempts. Root cause: the `mcp_stdio_watchdog.py` wrapper that intercepts the subprocess spawn breaks the stdio relay for `uvx`-spawned servers.

Gateway error log:

WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'aws' initial connection failed (attempt 1/3), retrying in 1s: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'aws' initial connection failed (attempt 2/3), retrying in 2s: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'aws' initial connection failed (attempt 3/3), retrying in 4s: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: Failed to connect to MCP server 'aws' (command=uvx): Connection closed

Same failure with `hermes mcp test aws` (10481ms, "Connection closed") and `hermes mcp add`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Add a uvx-based MCP server to config.yaml:
   yaml
  mcp_servers:
    aws:
      command: "uvx"
      args: ["awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server@latest"]
      enabled: true
      connect_timeout: 120
      env:
        PATH: "/opt/hermes/.venv/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
        READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY: "true"
        AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE: "/opt/data/.aws/credentials"
        AWS_CONFIG_FILE: "/opt/data/.aws/config"
        AWS_REGION: "eu-west-1"
        HOME: "/opt/data"

2. Restart gateway: supervisorctl restart hermes-gateway
3. Check logs: cat /var/log/supervisor/hermes-gateway-err.log | grep mcp
4. Also fails with: hermes mcp test aws and hermes
mcp add aws-test --command uvx --args awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server@latest

PS: I'm running Hermes inside a docker container, that's why the aws paths are not the default ones and I'm using supervisor to run the binaries.

### Expected Behavior

The uvx-based MCP server should connect successfully and register its tools, same as it does when called directly through the MCP SDK without the watchdog wrapper.

### Actual Behavior

Connection fails after 3 attempts with "Connection closed". The server never registers tools.

Isolated the failure to the watchdog:

# This WORKS (without watchdog):
params = StdioServerParameters(command='uvx', args=['awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server@latest'], env=safe_env)
async with stdio_client(params) as (read, write):
    async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
        result = await session.initialize()  # SUCCESS — 2 tools registered

# This FAILS (with watchdog — exactly what gateway does):
from tools.mcp_tool import _build_safe_env, _wrap_command_with_watchdog
command, args = _wrap_command_with_watchdog('uvx', ['awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server@latest'])
params = StdioServerParameters(command=command, args=args, env=safe_env)
async with stdio_client(params) as (read, write):
    async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
        result = await session.initialize()  # FAILS: Connection closed

Same failure for awslabs.eks-mcp-server@latest.

### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Running inside Docker container, cannot use hermes debug share. Manual info:
- Container: harbor.technest.es/fortris-platform/hermes-ui:latest
- Hermes: v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream f64e4f4f
- Python: 3.13.5
- uvx: 0.11.6
- MCP SDK: bundled with hermes
- Gateway managed by supervisord

PS: Debug report added below
```

### Operating System

Docker linux/amd64 (host: macOS arm64)

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Hermes Version

v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream f64e4f4f

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Full traceback when reproducing with watchdog in Python:

  | ExceptionGroup: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
  +-+---------------- 1 ----------------
    | ExceptionGroup: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
    +-+---------------- 1 ----------------
      | mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError: Connection closed
      +------------------------------------

Key observations:
- uvx @latest takes ~10s to start (network resolution before exec'ing Python entry point)
- connect_timeout: 120 is parsed correctly but doesn't help — failure isn't a timeout
- _build_safe_env correctly includes PATH
- The server responds to JSON-RPC initialize correctly when called without watchdog
- Same failure with eks-mcp-server (22s startup time)
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The bug is in `tools/mcp_stdio_watchdog.py` and its integration in `tools/mcp_tool.py` via `_wrap_command_with_watchdog()`.

The watchdog wraps the MCP server command as:
  python3 /opt/hermes/tools/mcp_stdio_watchdog.py --ppid <PID> --create-time <T> -- uvx awslabs.aws-api-mcp-server@latest

The watchdog uses subprocess.Popen with stdin/stdout piped and relays bytes between the MCP SDK's stdio transport and the actual server process. Something in this relay breaks for uvx-spawned servers that take ~10s to initialize (uvx resolves @latest over the network, downloads if needed, then exec's a shell wrapper script that finally runs Python).

Proof: identical environment, identical SDK calls — without _wrap_command_with_watchdog() it works, with it the connection drops.

Possibly related to #14113 (same symptom in gateway context, but that was attributed to stale CancelledError flags). The watchdog was likely introduced after that fix and reintroduces the failure through a different mechanism.

[debug-report.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30133081/debug-report.txt)

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Options:
1. Fix the watchdog's stdio relay to handle slow-starting uvx processes (the relay may be closing pipes prematurely when the child takes >Ns to produce its first stdout byte)
2. Add a per-server config option to disable the watchdog: `watchdog: false`
3. Skip the watchdog automatically for launcher commands (uvx, npx) that spawn their own managed child process — the watchdog's orphan-prevention rationale is already handled by uvx's own process management

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Desktop (Windows, no WSL): remote-gateway mode repeatedly spawns the "Install WSL" console window

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
When Hermes Desktop on Windows is connected to a **remote gateway** (a `hermes serve`
backend on a Linux VPS, reached through an SSH tunnel), the app repeatedly spawns
`wsl.exe`. On machines **without WSL installed**, each spawn opens the interactive
Windows console prompt:

> El Subsistema de Windows para Linux no está instalado. Para instalar, ejecute "wsl.exe --install".
> Presione cualquier tecla para instalar Subsistema de Windows para Linux...

This window keeps reappearing during normal use (roughly on every file-panel refresh),
even though no local backend is configured or needed.

## Environment

- **Client:** Hermes Desktop v0.18.2 (+11), Windows 11 Pro (build 26220), WSL **not** installed
- **Backend:** hermes serve v0.18.2 on Ubuntu 24.04 (remote VPS)
- **Connection mode:** Remote gateway → `http://localhost:9120` (SSH tunnel to VPS `127.0.0.1:9119`), token auth
- Connection itself works fine: chat, remote file tree, and terminal all operate against the VPS.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows machine **without** WSL installed.
2. Configure Hermes Desktop → Settings → Gateway → **Remote gateway**, URL + session token
   pointing at a `hermes serve` instance on a remote Linux host. Save and reconnect.
3. Use the app normally with the project/file panel visible (it lists the remote
   POSIX paths, e.g. `/home/ubuntu`).
4. A `C:\WINDOWS\system32\wsl.exe` console window with the "install WSL" prompt
   appears, and keeps reappearing periodically.

## Root cause (from a source read)

`apps/desktop/electron/wsl-path-bridge.ts` translates absolute POSIX paths to
`\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\...` UNC paths and calls `execFileSync('wsl.exe', ['-l', '-q'])`
to pick the default distro. It is reached from:

- `resolveLocalReadPath` → `apps/desktop/electron/fs-read-dir.ts` (file panel reads), and
- `resolvePickerDefaultPath` → `main.ts` (file-picker default path, `IS_WINDOWS` branch),
- plus `readWslWindowsClipboardImage` on clipboard operations.

None of these appear to be **gated on the resolved connection mode**. In remote-gateway
mode, POSIX paths coming from the remote backend are fed into the WSL bridge as if they
belonged to a local WSL backend, so `wsl.exe` is executed on a machine where WSL was never
required. (Observed parent chain also shows `svchost.exe -k P9RdrService` spawning
`wsl.exe` when `\\wsl$` UNC paths are touched.)

## Expected behavior

When the active connection is a remote gateway, POSIX paths should be resolved against
the remote backend (or the bridge should no-op), and `wsl.exe` should never be probed —
especially not in a way that pops an interactive install prompt on WSL-less machines.

## Workarounds found

- Hiding the file panel reduces the spawns.
- Installing the bare WSL platform (`wsl --install --no-distribution`) silences the
  prompt, since `wsl.exe -l -q` then exits quietly with no distros.

Happy to provide logs or test a patched build. Thanks!

items.title: [Bug]: System prompt hardcodes ~/.hermes, misdirecting the agent under a non-default HERMES_HOME

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

`agent/system_prompt.py` (`build_system_prompt_parts`) describes the agent's own filesystem layout using hardcoded `~/.hermes/...` literals rather than deriving it from `get_hermes_home()`. Under any non-default `HERMES_HOME` — the Docker default `/opt/data`, or profile mode where `HERMES_HOME` is `<root>/profiles/<name>` — the system prompt states paths that **do not exist**, and the agent believes them.

This is not cosmetic: the agent acts on the prompt. Ours repeatedly issued `search_files` against the non-existent path, failed with `Path not found`, and burned iterations (in some rounds exhausting its iteration budget without answering).

Notably, `hermes_constants.get_hermes_home()` already documents itself as the fix:
> Reads HERMES_HOME env var, falls back to `~/.hermes`. **This is the single source of truth — all other copies should import this.**

The tools (`browser_tool.py`, `browser_camofox*.py`, …) and the cross-profile guard (`agent/file_safety.py`) already import it. `agent/system_prompt.py` is the outlier that hardcodes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gateway with a non-default home, e.g. Docker `-e HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`.
2. Activate a named profile — `hermes_cli/profiles.py:1106` sets `os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = str(profile_dir)`, so `get_hermes_home()` → `/opt/data/profiles/coder`.
3. Ask the agent to look at its own skills / memories / plugins.
4. The prompt tells it to read `~/.hermes/profiles/coder/`, which resolves to a path that does not exist; the agent issues failing `search_files` calls.

## Expected Behavior

The system prompt names the agent's real directories, derived from `get_hermes_home()` / `get_default_hermes_root()`, so the agent looks in the right place.

## Actual Behavior

The prompt hardcodes `~/.hermes/...`. In our container (`HERMES_HOME=/opt/data`, profile mode):

```
EXISTS   /opt/data/profiles/coder          <- the real profile dir (== get_hermes_home())
MISSING  /opt/data/.hermes/profiles/coder  <- where the prompt sends the agent
MISSING  /root/.hermes                      <- literal ~/.hermes
```

The failure is independent of how `~` expands — neither `/root/.hermes` nor `/opt/data/.hermes` exists. The only correct value is `get_hermes_home()`.

## Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory) — specifically system-prompt assembly. Platform-agnostic (affects every profile/adapter, not a specific messaging platform).

## Debug Report

Not attached deliberately: this is a code-level defect fully determined by `agent/system_prompt.py` + the value of `HERMES_HOME`, reproducible from source without runtime state, and we would rather not upload a self-hosted deployment's config/logs to a public paste. Everything needed to reproduce is above. Happy to provide more on request.

## Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) container, on Ubuntu 24.04 host.

## Python Version

3.13.5

## Hermes Version

0.15.1

## Additional Logs / Traceback

```
Tool search_files returned error: {"total_count": 0,
  "error": "Path not found: /opt/data/.hermes/profiles/coder"}
Tool search_files returned error: {"total_count": 0,
  "error": "Path not found: /opt/data/.hermes/profiles/coder/skills"}
```

## Root Cause Analysis

`agent/system_prompt.py` hardcodes the default layout in four places inside `build_system_prompt_parts`:

- **L250** (default branch): `"...Other profiles (if any) live under ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/..."`
- **L259** (named-profile branch): `f"...This session reads and writes ~/.hermes/profiles/{active_profile}/..."`
- **L260–261**: `f"...The default profile's data lives at ~/.hermes/skills/, ~/.hermes/plugins/, ~/.hermes/cron/, ~/.hermes/memories/..."`

The module does not import `hermes_constants`, so it has no way to know the real home.

Two knock-on effects worth noting:
- The **cross-profile isolation guidance** lives in this same string. The prompt tells the agent not to touch other profiles' `skills/plugins/cron/memories` and names them by path — under a non-default home those paths are wrong, so the safety instruction points at locations that don't exist while the real ones go unnamed. (The *enforcement* in `agent/file_safety.py` is unaffected — it resolves real paths — so this is a "the agent is misinformed" bug, not a data-safety bug.)

## Proposed Fix

Derive the paths from the existing helpers, matching `agent/file_safety.py`. Both helpers already exist in `hermes_constants`:
- `get_hermes_home()` → this session's own dir (the profile dir in profile mode)
- `get_default_hermes_root()` → the profiles root / default-profile data

```diff
     TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS,
 )
+from hermes_constants import get_default_hermes_root, get_hermes_home

@@ default-profile branch
         stable_parts.append(
             "Active Hermes profile: default. Other profiles (if any) live "
-            "under ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/. Each profile has its own "
+            f"under {get_default_hermes_root()}/profiles/<name>/. Each profile has its own "
             ...

@@ named-profile branch
     else:
+        _root = get_default_hermes_root()
         stable_parts.append(
             f"Active Hermes profile: {active_profile}. This session reads "
-            f"and writes ~/.hermes/profiles/{active_profile}/. The default "
-            f"profile's data lives at ~/.hermes/skills/, ~/.hermes/plugins/, "
-            f"~/.hermes/cron/, ~/.hermes/memories/ — those belong to a "
+            f"and writes {get_hermes_home()}/. The default "
+            f"profile's data lives at {_root}/skills/, {_root}/plugins/, "
+            f"{_root}/cron/, {_root}/memories/ — those belong to a "
             ...
```

Verified against 0.15.1: applies, compiles, and renders correct paths (e.g. `writes /opt/data/profiles/coder/`).

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes — happy to open a PR with this change.

items.title: Feature: MCP Smart Loading — Lazy Connection, Tool Budget, Per-Session Scoping & On-Demand Servers

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
## Umbrella Issue

**Related issues:** #63626 (lazy MCP), #6839 (tool schema deferral), #45955 (per-session tool scoping, ACP)
**Labels:** `type/feature`, `tool/mcp`, `comp/tools`, `comp/agent`

---

## Problem

Hermes connects **every** `enabled: true` MCP server at startup, registers all their tools, and injects every tool schema into the LLM system prompt on every API call. For users with many MCP servers (18+ is common in homelab setups), this causes:

1. **Slow startup** — every `npx -y <package>` cold-start, every HTTP handshake, every subprocess spawn happens before the first message
2. **Wasted resources** — servers for rarely-used domains consume memory and startup time even when the session never touches them
3. **Context window bloat** — 18 servers × 5-20 tools each = 90-360 extra tool schemas on every API call, burning tokens and degrading prompt cache
4. **No per-task tailoring** — you can't scope which MCP servers are active for the current task

The current workarounds are inadequate:
- `enabled: false` + manual `/reload-mcp` — breaks prompt cache, requires remembering to enable
- `idle_timeout_seconds` — reconnects on-demand, but only *after* the first eager connection
- `no_mcp` sentinel in platform toolsets — all-or-nothing per platform

---

## Proposed Solution: Four Levers

### Lever 1: `connect_strategy` — Per-Server Connection Timing

Add a config field per server with three modes:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  cloudflare:
    url: https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp
    connect_strategy: startup    # default — connect at startup (current behavior)

  immich:
    command: npx
    args: [-y, immich-mcp]
    connect_strategy: lazy       # register schemas, defer subprocess spawn

  letsfg:
    command: npx
    args: [-y, letsfg-mcp]
    connect_strategy: on_demand  # invisible until explicitly loaded
```

**`startup`** (default, backward compatible): Current behavior — connect during `discover_mcp_tools()`, register tools, inject schemas.

**`lazy`**: Register tool schemas at startup (LLM can see the tools exist) but do NOT spawn the subprocess. On first tool call, connect synchronously then forward. Reuses the existing reconnect machinery (`_reconnect_event`, `_ready`, `connect_timeout`).

**`on_demand`**: Do NOT register tool schemas at startup. A meta-tool `mcp_load_server` lets the LLM (or user via `/mcp load`) activate a server mid-session.

### Lever 2: Tool Schema Budget — Cap Context Window Bloat

```yaml
mcp:
  tool_budget: 50   # max MCP tool schemas in the prompt (default: 0 = unlimited)
```

When the total MCP tools exceed the budget:
- **Priority ordering**: servers with `priority: high` are always included
- **LRU eviction**: least-recently-used servers' tools are dropped from the schema
- **Fallback meta-tool**: `mcp_list_servers` and `mcp_load_server` let the LLM discover and activate servers on its own

### Lever 3: Per-Session MCP Selection — Slash Commands

```
/mcp list              → show all servers, their status, tool counts, and strategy
/mcp enable <name>     → add server's tools to current session
/mcp disable <name>    → remove server's tools from current session
/mcp load <name>       → force-connect a lazy/on_demand server now
```

Toolset filtering happens at the `get_tool_definitions()` level — the server stays connected, but its schemas are excluded from the prompt.

### Lever 4: Meta-Tools for Agent-Driven Discovery

**`mcp_list_servers`** — returns all configured servers with name, transport, connection status, tool count, strategy, and whether tools are active.

**`mcp_load_server`** — activates a lazy or on_demand server: connects if needed, registers tools, returns newly available tool names.

This lets the agent self-discover: "I need to look up a flight" → calls `mcp_list_servers` → sees `letsfg` is on_demand → calls `mcp_load_server("letsfg")` → uses its tools.

---

## Implementation Sketch

### Files to modify

| File | Changes |
|---|---|
| `tools/mcp_tool.py` | Parse `connect_strategy`; gate connection in `discover_mcp_tools()`; wrap lazy handlers with connection gate; add `mcp_list_servers` and `mcp_load_server` tools |
| `hermes_cli/tools_config.py` | Apply `mcp.tool_budget` cap in `_get_platform_tools()`; LRU tracking for eviction |
| `hermes_cli/commands.py` | Add `/mcp` slash command family |
| `cli.py` | Wire `/mcp` command handlers |
| `hermes_cli/config.py` | Add `mcp.tool_budget` and `mcp.connect_strategy` defaults |
| `model_tools.py` | Pass tool budget to tool definition assembly |
| `tools/registry.py` | Support per-session tool visibility toggling |

### Key design decisions

1. **Default is `startup`** — backward compatible. Users opt servers into `lazy` or `on_demand`.
2. **Lazy connection reuses existing machinery** — `_request_lazy_reconnect()` already handles "wake dormant server and wait for `_ready`". The lazy-first-connect case is the same state machine with a new initial state.
3. **Tool budget is a soft cap** — it limits schemas in the prompt, not tool registration. The registry always has all tools; the prompt builder selects a subset.
4. **Per-session scoping is ephemeral** — `/mcp enable/disable` lasts for the current session only. No config file mutation.
5. **`mcp_list_servers` and `mcp_load_server` are always available** — even when all MCP tools are evicted by the budget, these meta-tools remain so the agent can recover.

---

## Backward Compatibility

- `connect_strategy` defaults to `startup` — existing configs unchanged
- `mcp.tool_budget` defaults to `0` (unlimited) — existing behavior preserved
- `/mcp` commands are additive — no existing workflow broken
- `enabled: false` still works as before (server is skipped entirely)
- `idle_timeout_seconds` / `max_lifetime_seconds` still work for recycling connected servers

---

## Related Issues

- **#63626** — `lazy: true` for MCP servers (narrower scope: lazy connection only)
- **#6839** — Lazy tool schema loading (two-pass, core tools focus)
- **#45955** — ACP per-session tool scoping (ACP-only, not CLI/gateway)
- **#13332** — Hybrid RAG tool pre-selection (complementary: semantic selection could replace LRU eviction)

items.title: A UTF-16 .env silently corrupts the first key - and the sanitizer writes the corruption back to disk

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Impact

Saving `~/.hermes/.env` as **Unicode (UTF-16 LE + BOM)** from Windows Notepad (or any editor that writes UTF-16) causes Hermes to **silently drop the first env key** and then **permanently rewrite the on-disk file in a mangled form**.

- No error is raised.
- Canonical `os.environ.get("HERMES_TEST_KEY")` returns `None`.
- The first key appears under a mangled name like `\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY`.
- On the next startup, the sanitizer has already rewritten the file with U+FFFD bytes baked in (`EF BF BD EF BF BD...`), so the corruption **survives** even if the user later opens the file in a UTF-8 editor.

This is worse than a pure load bug: the pre-load sanitizer **persists** the damage.

## Byte-level repro (macOS / Linux; emulates Notepad "Unicode")

Against current `main` (`bcea5371c`):

```python
import codecs, os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from hermes_cli.env_loader import load_hermes_dotenv

home = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
env = home / ".env"
content = "HERMES_TEST_KEY=hello_utf16\nSECOND_KEY=world\n"
env.write_bytes(codecs.BOM_UTF16_LE + content.encode("utf-16-le"))

os.environ.pop("HERMES_TEST_KEY", None)
os.environ.pop("SECOND_KEY", None)
load_hermes_dotenv(hermes_home=home)

print("canonical:", repr(os.environ.get("HERMES_TEST_KEY")))
print("mangled  :", repr(os.environ.get("\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY")))
print("on disk  :", env.read_bytes()[:40].hex())
```

### Observed before fix

| Encoding | Canonical first key | Mangled key | On-disk after load |
|----------|---------------------|-------------|--------------------|
| UTF-16-LE + BOM | `None` | `\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY=hello_utf16` | rewritten: starts `ef bf bd ef bf bd...` |
| UTF-16-BE + BOM | `None` | same class of mangling | rewritten mangled |
| UTF-16-LE no BOM | loads (accidental) | n/a | often repaired via NUL strip |
| UTF-16-BE no BOM | loads (accidental) | n/a | often repaired via NUL strip |

Mangled key name (LE+BOM, after rewrite) is literally U+FFFD U+FFFD glued to the original key: `\ufffd\ufffdHERMES_TEST_KEY` with value `hello_utf16`.

## Mechanism

`_sanitize_env_file_if_needed` (was lines ~167-217 on `main`) does:

1. `open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", errors="replace")`
2. For a UTF-16 BOM (`FF FE` / `FE FF`), those two bytes are not a UTF-8 BOM, so they become **two U+FFFD replacement characters** glued to the first key name.
3. Embedded NUL bytes (the other half of every UTF-16 code unit for ASCII) are stripped.
4. Because `sanitized != original`, the result is written back with `mkstemp` + `fsync` + `atomic_replace` as UTF-8, **permanently** storing the U+FFFD-prefixed key.

BOM-less UTF-16 of pure ASCII happens to look like NUL-padded ASCII; the existing NUL strip path accidentally "repairs" it. That is coincidence, not a design.

## Relationship to #65123 / #65124

**Sibling, not duplicate.**

| | #65123 / #65124 | This issue |
|--|-----------------|------------|
| Encoding | UTF-8 + BOM (`EF BB BF`) | UTF-16 + BOM (`FF FE` / `FE FF`) |
| Root cause | `load_dotenv(encoding="utf-8")` keeps U+FEFF on the first key | **Sanitizer** decode with `errors=replace` then **rewrite** |
| Disk mutation | No (load-time only) | **Yes** - file permanently mangled |
| Fix surface | `_load_dotenv_with_fallback` (+ send_cmd) | `_sanitize_env_file_if_needed` |

#65248 is UTF-8 BOM only in sanitize (related but not UTF-16).

Cross-link: #65123

## Environment

- Python: 3.11 (venv `python3.11`)
- hermes-agent: 0.18.2 (`pyproject.toml`)
- python-dotenv: 1.2.2
- OS: macOS (Darwin arm64)

## Platform honesty

Repro is **byte-level emulation** of Notepad "Unicode" / UTF-16-LE+BOM and UTF-16-BE+BOM (and BOM-less variants). PowerShell 5.1 and Notepad were **not** executed on a Windows host in this run.

## Expected behavior

- UTF-16 (with BOM) `.env` should load the first key under its **canonical** name.
- On-disk file should be rewritten as **clean UTF-8** (no BOM, no U+FFFD), or left untouched if the encoding is unsupported (e.g. UTF-32: refuse-to-mangle).
- Never persist `errors=replace` garbage back to disk.

items.title: save_env_value writes unquoted values with internal spaces - breaks shell-sourcing of .env (core-writer sibling of #57247)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Impact (first)

Real flows write **filesystem paths that routinely contain spaces** into `~/.hermes/.env` via the core writer `save_env_value` → `_quote_env_value`:

| Flow | Env key | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| `hermes setup` → SSH backend | `TERMINAL_SSH_KEY` | `hermes_cli/setup.py` (~1416) `save_env_value("TERMINAL_SSH_KEY", ssh_key)` |
| Google Chat setup | `GOOGLE_CHAT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` | `plugins/platforms/google_chat/adapter.py` (~3484) |
| `hermes config set TERMINAL_SSH_KEY …` / `terminal.ssh_key` | same / via terminal env bridge | `set_config_value` → `save_env_value` (`hermes_cli/config.py`) |

**macOS is most exposed**: paths under `~/Library/Application Support/...` are common for keys and service-account JSON. Windows `Program Files` / user profile spaces are also in-scope when those paths are saved through the same writer.

## Repro (upstream/main @ `bcea5371c`)

Throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, real `save_env_value`:

```text
value = /Users/paulo/Library/Application Support/hermes/keys/id_ed25519
```

**Emitted line (verbatim):**
```text
TERMINAL_SSH_KEY=/Users/paulo/Library/Application Support/hermes/keys/id_ed25519
```

**python-dotenv:** OK — returns the full path (masks the bug for Hermes runtime load).

**Shell source:**
```bash
env -i sh -c 'set -a; . file; set +a'
```
**Exact error:**
```text
.env: line 1: Support/hermes/keys/id_ed25519: No such file or directory
```
(`TERMINAL_SSH_KEY` ends up empty / truncated after word-split.)

## Trigger condition (line numbers on this base)

`hermes_cli/config.py` `_quote_env_value` @ **7772**, used by `save_env_value` @ **7788**:

```python
needs_quoting = (
    "#" in value
    or '"' in value
    or "'" in value
    or value != value.strip()
)
```

Internal whitespace (space/tab between non-space characters) does **not** trigger quoting. Only `#`, quotes, or leading/trailing whitespace do.

## Why python-dotenv masks it

`python-dotenv` / `dotenv_values` treat unquoted values as running to EOL (modulo `#` comments). Shell `.` / `source` with `set -a` does POSIX word-splitting on unquoted assignment RHS / bare path fragments after the first space — so tools that shell-source `.env` (debug scripts, containers, `set -a; . ~/.hermes/.env`) break while Hermes itself keeps working.

## Class link (honest)

| Item | Surface | Status |
|------|---------|--------|
| **#57247** (accepted) | Installer writer for `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` | Bug accepted |
| **#57249** | Fixes **only** the installer (`install.sh` / `install.ps1`) | Does **not** touch `hermes_cli/config.py` |
| **#57449** | Competing installer-only PR | Same installer surface; **not** core serializer |
| **This issue** | **Core serializer** `_quote_env_value` / `save_env_value` | Sibling class: same unquoted-spaced-path failure mode, different write path |

#57249 is the right dialect (`\\` then `\"` then wrap) already used by `_quote_env_value`; the gap is the **trigger** missing internal whitespace, not the escape algorithm.

## Platform statement

- **Reproduced** on macOS with a real spaced path under Application Support.
- Failure mode is **POSIX shell sourcing**, not Hermes' primary dotenv load path.
- Fix is portable: quote when `any(c.isspace() for c in value)`; no install-script changes (those remain #57249's surface).

## Expected fix

Extend `needs_quoting` only (escaping/wrapping **unchanged**). Idempotent re-save; no mass-requote of unrelated `.env` keys on next write of a different key.

items.title: [Bug]: TUI enables DEC 2026 synchronized output inside Zellij, causing repeated/scrolling frames
items.body:
## Bug Description

When `hermes --tui` runs inside Zellij under an outer terminal that advertises DEC mode 2026 support (observed with WezTerm), old TUI frames can be visibly repeated into the main-screen scrollback. Large output blocks appear multiple times even though the model response and stored conversation contain only one copy.

The live rendering symptom is timing-sensitive, but the terminal-capability misdetection is deterministic: Hermes trusts the outer terminal's `TERM_PROGRAM=WezTerm` while a Zellij multiplexer layer is present.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Zellij from WezTerm, or otherwise reproduce the relevant environment:

   ```shell
   TERM_PROGRAM=WezTerm
   ZELLIJ=0
   TMUX=<unset>
   ```

2. Run `hermes --tui`.
3. Generate a long response or another sequence with frequent frame/status updates.
4. Observe old output blocks occasionally being pushed into scrollback/repeated during redraws.

The capability bug can be reproduced reliably with this regression test:

```ts
process.env.TERM_PROGRAM = 'WezTerm'
process.env.ZELLIJ = '0'
delete process.env.TMUX

const { isSynchronizedOutputSupported } = await import('./terminal.js')

expect(isSynchronizedOutputSupported()).toBe(false)
```

On unpatched upstream code the assertion fails because the function returns `true`.

## Expected Behavior

Hermes should not trust an outer terminal's DEC 2026 capability when running through Zellij. `isSynchronizedOutputSupported()` and the module-level `SYNC_OUTPUT_SUPPORTED` value should both be `false` when `ZELLIJ` is set.

Each TUI frame should render once without copying prior output blocks into scrollback.

## Actual Behavior

`isSynchronizedOutputSupported()` only excludes tmux. With `TERM_PROGRAM=WezTerm` and `ZELLIJ=0`, it returns `true`, so Hermes wraps TUI frame writes in BSU/ESU synchronized-output markers even though the intervening multiplexer can parse, proxy, or chunk the stream independently.

The resulting visual corruption looks like repeated model output, but the underlying response/session data is not duplicated.

## Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat), specifically the Ink-based `hermes --tui` renderer under `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink`.

## Messaging Platform

N/A (CLI only)

## Debug Report

Not uploaded: there is no crash or application traceback, and the issue is isolated to deterministic terminal-capability detection. Uploading the general debug bundle would include unrelated local configuration/log data. Relevant environment and validation results are included below.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux 6.8.0 x86_64
- Python: 3.11.15
- Zellij: 0.44.3
- Outer terminal: WezTerm
- Hermes installation: git
- Currently installed Hermes: v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Still present in upstream `main` at `bcea5371c8194097e867cc0d49a97e7eb958c5df`

The original visual failure was observed on 2026-07-05. The exact Hermes version from that run was not captured; the same unguarded capability logic remains in current upstream `main`.

## Root Cause Analysis

The problem is in `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/terminal.ts`:

```ts
export function isSynchronizedOutputSupported(): boolean {
  if (process.env.TMUX) {
    return false
  }

  const termProgram = process.env.TERM_PROGRAM

  if (termProgram === 'WezTerm' /* ... */) {
    return true
  }
}
```

Zellij exposes `ZELLIJ` (observed as the string `"0"`) but Hermes does not check it. The inherited outer-terminal identity therefore wins, even though the renderer is not writing directly to that terminal.

This is the same general failure mode already documented for tmux: synchronized-output markers can reach the outer terminal after the multiplexer has already broken frame atomicity by processing/chunking the stream.

## Proposed Fix

Treat Zellij like tmux in the synchronized-output capability check:

```ts
if (process.env.TMUX || process.env.ZELLIJ) {
  return false
}
```

Add a regression test covering both the direct WezTerm case (`true`) and WezTerm through Zellij (`false`).

A local patch with this change was validated with:

- `npx vitest run packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/terminal.test.ts`
- `npx vitest run packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/log-update.test.ts packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/ink-backpressure.test.ts packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/ink-resize.test.ts` (15 tests passed)
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run build`
- Long-output smoke test inside Zellij; no repeated blocks were observed after the patch

## Related Issues / PRs

- #17961 — Ink/TUI ghost copies after terminal resize
- #19216 — Ink/TUI infinite scroll/render loop and duplicated status bar
- #8688 — status bar duplication specific to another terminal multiplexer (cmux)
- #21373 — terminal/multiplexer capability detection platform
- #48982 — disables a TUI fast path inside tmux because the multiplexer desynchronizes the renderer's cursor model
- #59423 is superficially similar but appears to duplicate the assistant message object; this report is about terminal frame rendering/scrollback, not conversation data

## PR Availability

A tested local patch and regression test are available, but I am not committing to a PR in this issue.

labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
Problem

Hermes only "compacts" when hitting the hard context limit, at which point it silently drops the oldest messages — whether or not those messages still matter. Long sessions degrade as useful early context gets evicted alongside noise.

Proposed Solution

Periodic context scan (triggered by token count approaching a soft limit, e.g. 80% of max) that:

1. Scores each message by recency, tool-use dependency, and user reference
2. Compacts low-value messages: old tool outputs already acted on, verbose intermediate steps, repeated error loops
3. Replaces them with a single summary line: ⁠[compacted: N messages, key facts preserved below]⁠
4. Preserves all user messages and any message referenced by a later tool call

Why This Works

 Agent decides what's disposable, not a hardcoded age cutoff
 Preserves reasoning chain integrity — no more losing the setup because the punchline was newer
 Summary line gives the LLM a hook to re-expand if needed via ⁠session_search⁠

Implementation

 Add compaction check after each agent turn (post-tool, pre-next-call)
 Token counter integration (existing tiktoken/estimation)

 Scoring heuristic: user messages = always keep, tool results = keep if re-read within last N turns, assistant reasoning = keep if < M turns old
 Compacted output saved to ⁠~/.hermes/compaction/<session-id>.jsonl⁠ for full audit trail
 Config: ⁠soft_limit_ratio⁠ (default 0.8), ⁠min_messages_before_compact⁠ (default 20)

items.title: stdio MCP watchdog kills every healthy child on WSL2: exact create_time equality breaks on btime drift

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary

On WSL2 (and likely any VM whose clock resyncs after a host sleep), `tools/mcp_stdio_watchdog.py::_is_orphaned` kills **every healthy stdio MCP child ~2 seconds after spawn**, forever. The result is an endless `keepalive failed → reconnect` churn every `keepalive_interval` (~190s wall-clock per cycle), and agents see `ClosedResourceError` on every in-session MCP tool call while a manually spawned server works fine. `tui_gateway/slash_worker.py::_is_orphaned` has the same defect.

## Root cause

The PID-reuse guard compares the parent's psutil creation time with **exact float equality**:

```python
return psutil.Process(original_ppid).create_time() != parent_create_time
```

On Linux, `create_time = /proc/stat btime + starttime/CLK_TCK`. On WSL2, `btime` shifts by a few seconds when the kernel clock resyncs (typically after Windows sleep/hibernate). Once that happens, the long-running gateway keeps passing a `--create-time` computed under the *old* btime, while every freshly spawned watchdog reads the *new* btime. The constant nonzero delta makes `_is_orphaned` return True on the watchdog's first 2s poll → `_terminate_process_group(proc)` SIGTERMs the healthy server. Silently: nothing reaches `mcp-stderr.log`, and the keepalive only notices the corpse up to `keepalive_interval` later.

## Evidence (caught in the act)

Gateway pid 6940, alive the whole time. Watchdog cmdline vs live psutil read:

```
$ ps -eo pid,ppid,cmd | grep mcp_stdio_watchdog
24930  6940 ... mcp_stdio_watchdog.py --ppid 6940 --create-time 1784317230.51 -- ...

$ venv/bin/python -c "import psutil; print(psutil.Process(6940).create_time())"
1784317227.51        # constant 3.0s delta — btime shifted after a Windows sleep
```

`errors.log` signature (both stdio servers, every ~190s = 180s keepalive + reconnect overhead, for days):

```
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'tradingview' keepalive failed, triggering reconnect:
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'open-second-brain' keepalive failed, triggering reconnect:
```

(the exception message is empty — the ping hits an already-closed transport instantly, i.e. the child died long before the probe).

Process polling confirmed each child lived <8s after "starting MCP server", while the same server spawned by hand (initialize + ping over stdio) stays up indefinitely.

## Fix suggestion

Use a tolerance instead of equality — real PID reuse differs by minutes-to-days, so a small window loses no protection:

```python
_CREATE_TIME_TOLERANCE_S = 30.0  # WSL2/VM btime drift after host-clock resync

return abs(psutil.Process(original_ppid).create_time() - parent_create_time) > _CREATE_TIME_TOLERANCE_S
```

Applied locally to both `tools/mcp_stdio_watchdog.py` and `tui_gateway/slash_worker.py`; verified the next reconnect cycle produced a child that survived 390s+ (two keepalive cycles, pings green) where before it died at ~2s every cycle.

## Environment

- Hermes agent on WSL2 (Ubuntu) under Windows 11, gateway + TUI sessions
- psutil 7.2.2, stdio MCP servers (Python FastMCP and others — affects all stdio servers equally)
- Trigger condition: any WSL2 kernel clock resync after gateway start (e.g. host sleep/resume)

items.title: Feature request: session-start hook to run a command/check before the first turn

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
**Problem**

There's currently no way to have Hermes run a live command or check automatically at the *start* of every session, before the model sees the user's first message. The only "auto-loaded at session start" mechanisms are static text injection:

- Project context files (`.hermes.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`) — injected into the system prompt, but only static text, and only when Hermes runs with a matching cwd.
- `SOUL.md` — global, but also static text only.
- Cron jobs — run in their own isolated session, can't inject into the interactive session.
- Skills — only load when explicitly invoked/matched, not guaranteed at session start.

There's no hook point to actually *execute* something (a shell command, a config read, an API call) and have its live output show up before/alongside the system prompt on session start.

**Motivating use case**

I'm building a skill that should behave differently depending on which model is currently active for the session (e.g. be more aggressive about offloading work to a local LLM when the active Hermes model is a cheap/budget tier vs. a frontier one). Right now this only works reliably if the skill happens to get invoked in that session — there's no way to guarantee the check runs at session start regardless of what the user asks first.

**Requested feature**

A `session_start` hook (analogous to a pre-prompt/pre-flight hook) that:
- Runs once per new session (respects `/new`, `/reset`, gateway session boundaries, etc.)
- Can execute a user-configured command/script (or a lightweight built-in check like "active model name")
- Injects the *live* output into the system prompt or as a synthetic tool-result/context message, not just static file content
- Is configurable per-profile (`config.yaml`, e.g. `session.start_hook: /path/to/script.sh`)

Even a minimal version — just exposing the resolved active model/provider name as a first-class fact always visible in context (today this is implicit/inconsistent depending on how the system prompt happens to be built) — would unblock the motivating use case without needing full arbitrary-command execution.

**Workaround currently used**

Relying on the fact that the active model name already appears somewhere in the agent's own system-prompt context each turn, and having a skill instruct the agent to self-check that instead of shelling out. Works, but it's fragile — it depends on the model choosing to read its own header correctly rather than a guaranteed, structured hook.

**Environment**

Hermes CLI, Nous Portal provider, Linux (CachyOS).

items.title: [Feature]: Per-call model/provider override for delegate_task

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Feature Description

Add optional `model` and `provider` parameters to `delegate_task`, allowing each subagent to use a different model than the global `delegation.model` config or the parent session model.

```python
delegate_task(
    goal="Audit security of auth module",
    context="...",
    model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4",      # per-call override
    provider="openrouter"                    # per-call override
)
```

## Motivation

Multi-agent systems benefit from heterogeneous models — one agent uses Claude for code review, another uses Gemini for vision tasks, a third uses DeepSeek for research. Today, all subagents share a single global `delegation.model` config. This forces users to:

- Spawn independent `hermes chat -m` processes (heavy, no built-in result merging)
- Create separate Hermes profiles per agent type (maintenance overhead)
- Manually route vision/compression tasks outside the subagent system

Users coming from Cursor/Cline/Roo Code are used to declaring per-agent models — this would make Hermes competitive for serious multi-agent workflows.

## Proposed Solution

1. `delegate_task` accepts optional `model` (string) and `provider` (string)
2. When set, they override `delegation.model`/`delegation.provider` for that specific subagent
3. When not set, the current behavior is preserved (delegation config → parent model)
4. Works for both single (`goal`) and batch (`tasks[]`) modes — per-task override takes priority

## Alternatives Considered

- **Profiles as workaround**: create a profile per model, spawn via `hermes --profile X`. Works but is heavy for teams with many specialized agents.
- **Cron jobs per model**: spawn a one-shot cron. Works but loses the tight feedback loop of `delegate_task`.

items.title: Custom-provider metadata probes ignore provider-scoped CA settings

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
## Problem

Per-provider `ssl_ca_cert` works for main and auxiliary model calls, but the custom endpoint metadata and pricing probes do not use it.

On current `main`, `agent.model_metadata.fetch_endpoint_model_metadata()` makes `requests.get()` calls with `_resolve_requests_verify()`. That resolver reads process-wide CA environment variables only:

```text
HERMES_CA_BUNDLE
REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE
SSL_CERT_FILE
```

It has no access to the selected custom provider's `ssl_ca_cert` or `ssl_verify` settings.

This creates split behavior for the same provider:

- Model calls succeed with the provider's configured CA bundle.
- `/models` metadata or pricing probes can fail certificate verification.
- The probe falls back to default metadata or pricing, so the warning can look unrelated to the working model request.

Changing a global CA environment variable avoids the failure but changes certificate handling for every provider. That defeats the purpose of provider-scoped TLS settings.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a custom HTTPS provider with `ssl_ca_cert` set to a CA bundle that validates its endpoint.
2. Leave the process-wide CA variables unset or pointed at a bundle that does not validate that endpoint.
3. Start a request that triggers endpoint metadata or pricing resolution.

Observed: the OpenAI/httpx client succeeds, while `fetch_endpoint_model_metadata()` fails TLS verification because it calls `_resolve_requests_verify()` without the provider settings.

Expected: probes for a configured custom provider should use the same resolved TLS policy as that provider's inference clients.

## Current code paths

- `agent/model_metadata.py::_resolve_requests_verify()` resolves only environment variables.
- `agent/model_metadata.py::fetch_endpoint_model_metadata()` uses it for `/models` and related probes.
- `agent/usage_pricing.py` calls `fetch_endpoint_model_metadata()` for custom routes.
- Merged PR #56681 added provider-scoped `ssl_ca_cert` support to main and auxiliary clients, but these `requests` probes remain outside that path.

## Suggested direction

Thread an explicit `verify` value or provider TLS settings into `fetch_endpoint_model_metadata()` and its callers. Reuse the existing custom-provider TLS resolver rather than adding another precedence chain.

Tests should cover both behaviors:

- An explicit provider CA is passed to the metadata probe.
- Unconfigured and public endpoints keep the current environment/default resolution.

items.title: [Bug] Local Ollama vision models (gemma4:31b + custom GGUFs) fail with "Failed to tokenize prompt" despite supports_vision: true and image_input_mode: "native"

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### Bug Description

When using local Ollama vision-capable models (official `gemma4:31b` as well as custom GGUFs such as Unsloth Gemma-4 quantizations) through Hermes, sending an image attachment results in:

```
HTTP 400: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Failed to tokenize prompt","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

Text-only messages work perfectly.  
Vision works correctly when the same models are used directly in pure Ollama (CLI / API).

This happens even after applying the known workarounds.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with a local Ollama provider (custom provider name `ollama-launch` pointing to `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`).
2. Set in `config.yaml`:

```yaml
model:
  supports_vision: true
  provider: ollama-launch
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1

agent:
  image_input_mode: "native"

providers:
  ollama-launch:
    supports_vision: true
    api: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
```

3. Restart Hermes completely.
4. Select a vision model (`gemma4:31b` or a custom Gemma-4 GGUF).
5. Attach any image and send a message (e.g. "was siehst du?").

### Expected Behavior

The image should be passed natively to the Ollama model as an `image_url` content part and the model should respond based on the visual content.

### Actual Behavior

Hermes returns:
```
Failed to tokenize prompt
```

The request never reaches a successful generation.

### Environment

- Hermes version: latest (as of 2026-07-17)
- Provider: custom (`ollama-launch`) → `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`
- Models tested:
  - Official `gemma4:31b`
  - Custom Unsloth Gemma-4 GGUFs (e.g. `gemma-4-31B-it_UD-Q4_K_XL`, `UD3`)
- OS: Windows
- Vision works in pure Ollama, fails only through Hermes

### Workarounds Tried

- `model.supports_vision: true`
- `agent.image_input_mode: "native"`
- `providers.ollama-launch.supports_vision: true`
- Per-model `supports_vision: true`
- Full Hermes restart after every config change

All of the above still result in the tokenize error.

Using an auxiliary vision model works, but is impractical for workflows that require permanent native vision (e.g. OCR-heavy profiles).

### Related Issues

- #54511
- #54593

### Additional Context

This appears to be a continuation of the known problem that Hermes does not correctly detect / route native vision for the local `ollama` provider (and custom OpenAI-compatible Ollama endpoints). The config overrides that should force native vision are currently ignored in this setup.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with a custom Ollama provider (`ollama-launch`) pointing to `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`
2. Set in config.yaml:
   - model.supports_vision: true
   - agent.image_input_mode: "native"
   - providers.ollama-launch.supports_vision: true
3. Fully restart Hermes
4. Select a vision model (official gemma4:31b or custom Gemma-4 GGUF)
5. Attach any image and send a message (e.g. "was siehst du?")

### Expected Behavior

The image should be passed natively to the Ollama model as an image_url content part. The model should analyze the image and respond based on the visual content.

### Actual Behavior

HTTP 400: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Failed to tokenize prompt","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

Text-only messages work fine. The same models work with vision when used directly in pure Ollama.

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

items.title: CI-sensitive file review fails on every fork PR: label fetch cannot read AUTOFIX_BOT_PAT

labels.name: sweeper:risk-automation
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect CI, automerge, label sync, or maintainer automation

items.body:
Since 597615ade landed (2026-07-17 ~20:55 UTC), the "Python lints / CI-sensitive file review" job fails on every pull request opened from a fork, at the "Fetch PR labels" step:

```
gh: To use GitHub CLI in a GitHub Actions workflow, set the GH_TOKEN environment variable.
##[error]failed after 3 attempts: gh pr view "NNNNN" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name'
```

Cause: the step authenticates with `secrets.AUTOFIX_BOT_PAT` (`.github/workflows/lint.yml:184`). GitHub withholds repository secrets from fork-origin `pull_request` runs, so `GH_TOKEN` is empty on fork PRs and `gh` exits 1 before the label check ever runs. The retry wrapper then fails the job, which fails the "All required checks pass" aggregate. Before 597615ade the fetch used `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, which is available to fork runs, inline with `|| true`.

Evidence that it is fork-specific and repo-wide rather than one branch:

- Fork PRs from different authors fail the same step: #66550, #66537, #38706, #36954, #44491.
- Same-repo PR #66528 passes "Fetch PR labels" (the secret resolves in-repo).
- The comment-posting steps in the same job are guarded with `head.repo.fork != true`; the fetch step has no fork guard, so this looks like an oversight rather than intent.

Suggested fix: `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.AUTOFIX_BOT_PAT || github.token }}` on the fetch step. Reading labels only needs the built-in read-only token, and the gate's decision still keys off the ci-reviewed label, which only maintainers can set.
