labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
# [Desktop] 点击侧边栏「新建会话」或 ⌘+N 会跳转到最近已有内容的会话，而不是新建空白会话

## 问题描述

在 Hermes Desktop 中，点击侧边栏的「新建会话」按钮（或使用快捷键 ⌘+N）时，没有创建新的空白会话，而是跳转/聚焦到了最近已有对话内容的会话窗口。

## 环境信息

- **Hermes Agent 版本**: v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream d59b79fa
- **安装方式**: git
- **操作系统**: macOS 26.3.1
- **Python**: 3.11.15
- **OpenAI SDK**: 2.24.0

## 复现步骤

1. 打开 Hermes Desktop。
2. 确保存在一个已有对话内容的会话（不是空会话）。
3. 点击侧边栏的「新建会话」按钮，或按下 ⌘+N 快捷键。
4. 观察到界面跳转到了最近的那个已有内容的会话，而不是新建空白会话。

## 预期行为

点击「新建会话」或 ⌘+N 应该创建一个新的、空的会话窗口，不应受最近会话是否存在内容的影响。

## 实际行为

点击「新建会话」或 ⌘+N 后，应用聚焦/跳转到了最近已有内容的会话，无法新建会话。

## 已尝试的排查

- 确认最近会话已有实际对话内容（非空会话）。
- 使用 ⌘+N 快捷键测试，行为与点击按钮一致。
- 确认不是空会话复用导致的假象。

## 临时绕过方案

在终端中执行 `hermes chat` 可以强制启动一个独立的全新 CLI 会话。

## 可能的根因猜测

Desktop 壳层（Electron/Tauri）将「新建会话」事件错误路由到了「恢复/聚焦最近会话」的逻辑，或最近 session ID 的缓存被错误地用于新会话创建。

items.title: cron: UTF-8 BOM in jobs.json crashes load_jobs (RuntimeError)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
# cron: UTF-8 BOM in jobs.json crashes load_jobs (RuntimeError)

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| OS | macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0 arm64) |
| Python | 3.11.15 |
| hermes | Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) |
| Base verified | `upstream/main` @ `d59b79fadd1e9edd7afc5c679cc3b143838e7c01` |

## Impact

A `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json` that starts with a UTF-8 BOM (byte sequence
`EF BB BF`) **fails to load**. Cron CRUD, due-job detection, and the
scheduler path that call `load_jobs()` raise:

```text
RuntimeError: Cron database corrupted and unrepairable: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

User-visible effects:

- Scheduled jobs stop running (scheduler cannot read the store).
- `hermes cron list` aborts with the RuntimeError above.
- `hermes status` prints `Jobs: (error reading jobs file)`.
- `hermes dump` prints `cron_jobs: (error reading)` instead of counts.

This is a **hard crash**, not a silent misparse — but it is easy to hit
after a Windows editor save of `jobs.json`.

## Full traceback (reproduced on upstream/main)

Throwaway `HERMES_HOME` (does not touch real `~/.hermes`). Python 3.11.15,
macOS Darwin 25.5.0, `upstream/main` @ `d59b79fad`:

```text
Failed to auto-repair jobs.json: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "cron/jobs.py", line 869, in load_jobs
    data = json.load(f)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../lib/python3.11/json/__init__.py", line 293, in load
    return loads(fp.read(),
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../lib/python3.11/json/__init__.py", line 335, in loads
    raise JSONDecodeError("Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig)",
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "cron/jobs.py", line 875, in load_jobs
    data = json.loads(f.read(), strict=False)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../lib/python3.11/json/__init__.py", line 335, in loads
    raise JSONDecodeError("Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig)",
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 5, in <module>
  File "cron/jobs.py", line 878, in load_jobs
    raise RuntimeError(f"Cron database corrupted and unrepairable: {e}") from e
RuntimeError: Cron database corrupted and unrepairable: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig): line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

Both the primary `json.load` open (`cron/jobs.py:868` on main) and the
`strict=False` auto-repair re-open (`cron/jobs.py:874`) fail on the same
BOM — repair cannot recover.

## Repro (throwaway HERMES_HOME)

```bash
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$TMP/cron"
printf '\xef\xbb\xbf{"jobs": []}\n' > "$TMP/cron/jobs.json"
HERMES_HOME="$TMP" python -c '
from cron.jobs import load_jobs
print(load_jobs())
'
# also: HERMES_HOME="$TMP" hermes cron list
# also: HERMES_HOME="$TMP" hermes status   # → Jobs: (error reading jobs file)
# also: HERMES_HOME="$TMP" hermes dump     # → cron_jobs: (error reading)
rm -rf "$TMP"
```

With `encoding="utf-8-sig"`: `load_jobs()` returns `[]` (or the job list);
`hermes cron list` / `status` / `dump` all succeed.

## Mechanism

Four independent readers open `jobs.json` with plain `encoding="utf-8"`
on `upstream/main` @ `d59b79fad`:

| Site | Role |
|------|------|
| `cron/jobs.py:868` `load_jobs` primary open | cron store |
| `cron/jobs.py:874` `load_jobs` strict=False retry | auto-repair arm |
| `hermes_cli/dump.py:170` `_cron_summary` | support dump |
| `hermes_cli/status.py:532` Scheduled Jobs | `hermes status` |

`json.load` under plain UTF-8 rejects a leading BOM. Writers already use
plain `utf-8` (no BOM on write), so the next successful `save_jobs()`
would heal a BOM'd file — but nothing can load it first.

## How BOMs get there

- Windows Notepad "UTF-8" save
- PowerShell 5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` (documented BOM-emitting
  dialect; PS 7+ differs)
- Some GUI editors / "UTF-8 with signature" exports

Hermes already documents BOM-aware reads for user-touched config in
CONTRIBUTING (`encoding="utf-8-sig"`). The env-class cluster (#65123)
is the same root cause on `.env` (silent key-drop); this issue is the
**crash** sibling for `jobs.json`.

## Expected fix

Read with `encoding="utf-8-sig"` on all four readers above. Leave writers on
plain `utf-8` so saves stay BOM-free.

## Scope of this issue

Only the four `jobs.json` readers listed above. Explicit non-scope
(follow-ups, not part of the fix for this issue):

- `hermes_cli/backup.py` `_count_cron_jobs` (still plain `utf-8`; under BOM
  count returns `None` → conservative skip, no false wipe)
- `agent/curator_backup.py` parse (snapshot copies raw bytes; parse_warning
  under BOM)
- Context-file BOM handling in `agent/prompt_builder.py` (separate path)

## Related

- #65123 — UTF-8 BOM in `.env` silently drops the first key (same BOM
  class; silent loss rather than crash)
- #10878 / #10879 / #53833 — MEMORY.md / memory BOM class (related
  encoding family; not this call site)
- #41604 — open PR that partially touches `cron/jobs.py` load_jobs BOM
  tolerance (plus unrelated prompt_builder); currently `DIRTY` vs main and
  does not cover the independent `dump` / `status` readers

## Platform

Any OS can load a BOM'd file authored on Windows or by a BOM-writing
tool. Most common authoring path is Windows Notepad / PS 5.1. Verified
crash on macOS with a synthetic BOM file.

items.title: [Bug]: "Already up to date" overlay's close (×) button is unresponsive and shows a stray red focus border
items.body:
## Bug Description
When the desktop app's update check returns "Already up to date" / "已是最新" (你正在运行最新版本), the only way to dismiss the overlay is the × button in the top-right of the dialog. Clicking it does nothing — the dialog stays on screen and blocks input to the rest of the app until the window is closed via the OS chrome. On top of that, the × button itself renders with an unexpected thick red border around it, which looks like an error / destructive state.

The red border around × looks like a stuck focus-ring or hover-state styling leaking into the default state — see the attached screenshot.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch the Hermes desktop app on Windows 11 (current `main` build).
2. Trigger an update check that resolves to "no update" — e.g. open the settings / About panel when already on the latest commit, or call `openUpdateOverlayFor('client')` from `updates.ts`.
3. Wait for the overlay to render the `IdleView` → `CenteredStatus` branch (the `!updateAvailable` arm that renders `BrandMark` + "已是最新" / "你正在运行最新版本。").
4. Click the × button in the top-right corner of the dialog.
5. Try clicking it multiple times, also try `Esc`, also try clicking the backdrop.

## Expected Behavior
- One click on × closes the overlay.
- `Esc` closes the overlay.
- Clicking the backdrop closes the overlay.
- × has no red border in its default (unfocused, unhovered) state.

## Actual Behavior
- × click does NOT close the overlay. Repeated clicks do nothing.
- `Esc` does not close it.
- × is surrounded by a clearly visible red rectangular border — looks like a styling bug, not the intended `--ring` focus state. Present even on first open before the user touches anything, not dependent on focus or hover.

## Affected Component
Desktop app (`apps/desktop/**`).

## Operating System
Windows 11 (latest stable channel). Not yet tested on macOS / Linux.

## Hermes Version
Current `main` build of `apps/desktop` at the time of filing.

## Debug Report
This bug does not emit a stack trace; it is purely a render + click-routing regression. No `hermes debug share` output is necessary. If reviewers want one, the overlay logs `setUpdateOverlayOpen(false)` to the renderer console whenever `.handleClose(false)` fires, so a console trace from DevTools is sufficient.

## Root Cause Analysis (best guess from reading the code)
The overlay lives at `apps/desktop/src/app/updates-overlay.tsx`:

```tsx
<Dialog onOpenChange={handleClose} open={open}>
  <DialogContent
    className="max-w-sm overflow-hidden p-0 gap-0"
    showCloseButton={phase !== 'applying'}
  >
    …
```

The relevant pieces:

- `phase === 'idle'` for the "已是最新" state, so `showCloseButton` is `true` and × should render.
- `handleClose(next)`:

  ```ts
  if (phase === 'applying') return
  setUpdateOverlayOpen(next)
  if (!next && (apply.stage === 'error' || …)) {
    resetUpdateApplyState()
  }
  ```

- The overlay has no explicit `onClose` / `onClick` on the close control itself, so dismissal depends entirely on the `Dialog` wrapper firing `onOpenChange(false)`.

Two things look fishy:

1. **Red focus border on ×.** The close icon is rendered by the shared `Dialog` / `DialogContent` wrapper. The default `--ring` (or whatever `focus-visible` style the design system applies via `button` from `@/components/ui/button`) is rendering as red against the white card. This is almost certainly a token-color regression where the focus ring is bound to `--destructive` / `--error` instead of `--ring`, and it is most visible on this dialog because the card is the whitest surface in the app. This part is a separate, purely visual regression that the user notices on every dialog × in the app, but this one is the most visually jarring.

2. **Click not closing.** Possible causes (in order of suspicion):
   - The shared `Dialog` wrapper swallows the × click when the inner content has no focusable affordances. `IdleView`'s `!updateAvailable` branch renders a `CenteredStatus` with **no buttons**, so the only focusable element inside the dialog is × itself. Some focus-trap libs misbehave when the trap has no focusable children beyond the supplied close control, especially if a parent `pointer-events: none` or `aria-hidden` is set on a wrapping element.
   - `phase` momentarily flicks to `'applying'` or is read from a stale ref when × is clicked, hitting `if (phase === 'applying') return` and silently dropping the click. (`UpdatesOverlay` uses `useStore` from `@nanostores/react` so this is unlikely, but worth ruling out.)
   - `useEffect(() => { if (open && !status && !checking) void check() }, …)` is racing with the close: opening fires the check, the check's promise resolves, `setUpdateOverlayOpen(true)` is called again, and the overlay snaps back open faster than the user can perceive it closing.

## Proposed Fix
Two changes, each addressing one of the two issues:

1. **Visual regression.** Audit the focus-ring token used by `DialogContent`'s built-in close button. Force it to `var(--ring)` (or whatever the design system's agreed focus color is) and never `var(--destructive)`. Verify no other dialog in the app shows the same red border. If the intent of the red border is something else (e.g. an indicator that the dialog is "destructive", which this dialog is not), document it and remove it here.

2. **Click-routing fix.** In `UpdatesOverlay`, do ALL of the following:

   ```ts
   const handleClose = (next: boolean) => {
     if (phase === 'applying') return
     console.debug('[updates] handleClose', { open, phase, applyStage: apply.stage, next })
     setUpdateOverlayOpen(next)
     …
   }

   useEffect(() => {
     if (open && !status && !checking && !apply.applying) {
       void check()
     }
   }, [check, checking, open, status, apply.applying])
   ```

   The `apply.applying` guard prevents the re-open race. If the close-routing issue persists, add an explicit `onClick` on the close control inside `DialogContent` (or whichever shared component renders ×) that calls `onOpenChange(false)` directly, so it is no longer dependent on whatever focus-trap or `aria-hidden` logic is swallowing the click.

## Contribution
- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Creating a new chat under a project sometimes creates a phantom duplicate session

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description
When starting a new chat from inside a project / worktree in the desktop app, intermittently an extra "ghost" session row appears in the sidebar alongside the intended one. The extra row usually has no title and no messages but persists across refreshes, and it cannot reliably be deleted on its own (deleting one removes the other, depending on luck). Most often it shows up empty with `<empty>`-style preview and clutters the sidebar until manually swept.

It happens:
- After clicking the "new chat" button while a project / worktree is attached.
- After selecting a project from the sidebar / workspace picker and then immediately hitting `n` / `Cmd+N` to start a new chat.
- After drag-and-dropping a folder onto the chat list to "attach" it and then starting a new chat.

The phantom row is always created in the SAME project folder as the legitimate one (it does not share cwd with the global default), which strongly suggests the create-on-attach flow is firing the create RPC twice.

## Steps to Reproduce (most reliable)
1. Launch Hermes desktop on Windows 11 with the current `main` build. Use the default profile.
2. Open an existing chat to seed the sidebar.
3. In the sidebar, switch to a project that has at least one prior session (a worktree is fine).
4. Click the "+" / "New chat" affordance **specific to the project view** (the affordance that scopes the new session to that worktree).
5. Wait ~300 ms (do not type anything yet).
6. Inspect `~/.hermes/state.db` (`hermes sessions list`), or just look at the sidebar.

### Expected Behavior
Exactly one new (empty) session row appears in the sidebar, scoped to that project, with the same `cwd` as the worktree.

### Actual Behavior
Two new empty rows appear, both with the same `cwd`, both with `preview: null` and `title: null` (or auto-title set shortly after). One of them is the "real" one that the composer is actually attached to; the other is detached and stale.

## Affected Component
Desktop app (`apps/desktop/**`); specifically the session-create + workspace-target machinery under `apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts`.

## Operating System
Windows 11 (reproduced reliably here; not yet tested on macOS / Linux).
Single-profile user, default project dir unset.

## Hermes Version
`main` build at the time of filing.

## Debug Report
This is a data-layer race; logs are helpful but optional. To capture, insert `console.debug('createNewSession', { project, generation })` at the createSession call site (look near `use-session-actions/index.ts` and the `setNewChatWorkspaceTarget` effect) and watch the renderer console while clicking "new chat under project" twice in a row — both invocations will be visible. There is no exception thrown; no `hermes debug share` is necessary.

## Root Cause Analysis (best guess)

Two upstream code paths can both call into "create a session in this project":

1. **`apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts` → `setNewChatWorkspaceTarget`:**

   ```ts
   export const setNewChatWorkspaceTarget = (next: NewChatWorkspaceTarget): number => {
     const generation = $newChatWorkspaceTargetGeneration.get() + 1
     $newChatWorkspaceTarget.set(next)
     $newChatWorkspaceTargetGeneration.set(generation)
     return generation
   }
   ```

   This uses a read-then-write counter to dedupe "set workspace + create session" cascades, but only races **among generators** — not among React strict-mode double-invocations. If two effects fire in the same tick with the same starting `gen=0` (a strict-mode double-mount, or attach-project + new-chat in the same microtask), **both** publish `gen=1`, and the downstream gate `if (gen === $newChatWorkspaceTargetGeneration.get())` lets **both** createSession calls through.

2. **`apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts` → `workspaceCwdForNewSession`:**

   ```ts
   return getRememberedWorkspaceCwd()
   ```

   The remembered workspace is updated as soon as the user attaches to a project. If the "attach project" path and the "new chat with current workspace" path both observe the new workspace before either has finished, **both** can fire `createSession` with the same cwd and the same parent worktree — yielding two empty rows with identical cwds.

The likely fix is to switch the workspace-target setter to a functional-form atom write and to coalesce the "new chat in project" action behind a "have I already created for this generation" ref. The existing tests in `apps/desktop/src/store/session.test.ts` are thorough about state and merges but do **not** cover the create-on-attach race, which is why this slipped through.

Related code worth pinning in the PR description:

- `apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/store/session.test.ts` (no current test for this race)
- `apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/` (create RPC call site)
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/sessions-section.tsx`

## Proposed Fix
Pick ONE of the following:

1. **Functional atom write + create-once-per-generation ref.** Replace `setNewChatWorkspaceTarget` with a functional update, and gate the createSession effect with `useRef<number | null>(null)` that records the last generation the effect fired for. Cheap, low-risk.

2. **Drop strict-mode double-invokes only.** Wrap the create-on-attach `useEffect` callback in a latched "have I already fired for this target" ref. Slightly less safe because it freezes future races of the same shape.

3. **Coalesce into one RPC.** Make the sidebar's "new chat in project" click fire `createSessionInWorkspace` directly, and delete the optimistic workspace-target → effect → createSession chain (the chain is no longer needed if the click is the single point of entry). Cleanest, most invasive.

Whichever you pick, add a regression test in `session.test.ts`:

```ts
it('does not create a phantom session when setNewChatWorkspaceTarget is invoked twice synchronously', () => {
  const created: unknown[] = []
  // stub the create RPC + fire the setter twice synchronously
  setNewChatWorkspaceTarget(workspaceA)
  setNewChatWorkspaceTarget(workspaceA) // React-18 strict-mode double-invoke
  // assert created.length === 1
})
```

## Contribution
- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: gateway.api_server config.yaml section is ignored during gateway initialization
items.body:
### Bug Description

When configuring the Hermes API Server through `config.yaml`, the `gateway.api_server` section is ignored during gateway initialization.

The API Server only starts when environment variables such as `API_SERVER_ENABLED` and `API_SERVER_KEY` are set.

Other gateway subsections (for example `gateway.streaming`) are processed correctly, making `gateway.api_server` inconsistent with the rest of the gateway configuration.

I investigated the issue, traced the initialization path, identified the root cause in `gateway/config.py`, prepared a minimal patch, and verified it through runtime testing.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the gateway using YAML only:

```yaml
gateway:
  api_server:
    enabled: true
    port: 8642
```

2. Ensure no `API_SERVER_ENABLED` or `API_SERVER_KEY` environment variables are set.

3. Start the Hermes gateway.

4. Observe that the API Server is skipped during startup.

5. Port 8642 never starts listening.

6. Set the equivalent environment variables and restart.

7. Observe that the API Server now starts successfully.

### Expected Behavior

The gateway should parse the gateway.api_server configuration from config.yaml and initialize Platform.API_SERVER in the same way other gateway subsections are processed.

### Actual Behavior

The gateway completely ignores gateway.api_server during configuration loading.

Platform.API_SERVER is never created from YAML configuration.

The API Server only starts when enabled through environment variables.

### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
No hermes debug report was generated for this investigation.

The issue was reproduced through source-code tracing, runtime verification, upstream comparison, and gateway logs.

I can provide logs and the validated patch if needed.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Current upstream main (verified against the latest source available during investigation)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Gateway startup log:

API_SERVER_KEY is required for the API server.

The API Server platform is skipped during initialization when only YAML configuration is provided.

Port 8642 never opens.

When the equivalent environment variables are set, the API Server starts normally.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The issue originates in `gateway/config.py`.

`load_gateway_config()` processes several gateway subsections, including:

- gateway.streaming
- gateway.max_concurrent_sessions
- gateway.multiplex_profiles

However, `gateway.api_server` is never parsed.

As a result, no `Platform.API_SERVER` configuration is created from YAML.

Later, `_apply_env_overrides()` only checks environment variables, which explains why the API Server works only when enabled through environment variables.

I compared this against the latest upstream source and confirmed that no equivalent implementation currently exists.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add handling for the missing `gateway.api_server` subsection in `load_gateway_config()`.

The implementation mirrors the existing `gateway.streaming` configuration handling, preserving the current environment-variable precedence and introducing no behavior changes outside this configuration path.

The fix has been validated through:

- source-code verification
- runtime verification
- upstream comparison
- regression testing
- MCP validation

I have a production-ready patch prepared and would be happy to submit a Pull Request if this approach is acceptable.

items.title: [Bug]%20_resolve_task_provider_model%20ignores%20key_env%20field%20in%20auxiliary%20task%20config%20%E2%86%92%20vision/compression%20401

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

`_resolve_task_provider_model()` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py` reads `api_key` from the auxiliary task config but **never reads `key_env`** (or `api_key_env`). When a user configures an auxiliary task with `key_env` instead of a plaintext `api_key`, the resolved API key is `None`, and requests are sent with the `"no-key-required"` placeholder → `401 AuthenticationError` on every call.

## Reproduction

```yaml
# ~/.hermes/config.yaml
auxiliary:
  vision:
    provider: custom
    model: qwen3.7-plus
    base_url: https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1
    key_env: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY      # ← this field is NEVER parsed
    timeout: 120
```

```bash
# .env has the key
DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=sk-sp-xxxxxxxxxxxx
```

```python
# vision_analyze tool fails every time:
# openai.AuthenticationError: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'code': 'invalid_api_key', ...}}
```

## Root Cause

`agent/auxiliary_client.py`, function `_resolve_task_provider_model()` (line ~5888):

```python
cfg_api_key = str(task_config.get("api_key", "")).strip() or None
# ← key_env is never consulted here
cfg_api_mode = str(task_config.get("api_mode", "")).strip() or None
```

The `key_env` field **is** correctly parsed in two other places in the same file:
- `_fallback_entry_api_key()` (L3987) — reads `key_env`/`api_key_env`
- named custom provider resolution (L4721) — reads `key_env`/`api_key_env`

But the top-level auxiliary task config resolution path in `_resolve_task_provider_model()` does not.

## Impact

Any auxiliary task (`vision`, `compression`, `web_extract`, `session_search`) configured with `key_env` instead of inline `api_key` will fail with 401. This is the documented/recommended way to configure credentials (keeping secrets in `.env`, not `config.yaml`), so users following best practices hit this bug.

Related issues:
- #9318 — similar symptom (no-key-required fallback) but different root cause (wants to inherit `model.api_key`)
- #16254 — mentions `key_env never parsed in aux config` as a side note

## Fix

Add `key_env` resolution in `_resolve_task_provider_model()` right after reading `cfg_api_key`:

```python
cfg_api_key = str(task_config.get("api_key", "")).strip() or None
# Resolve key_env → env var if api_key is not set directly
if not cfg_api_key:
    cfg_key_env = str(task_config.get("key_env") or task_config.get("api_key_env") or "").strip()
    if cfg_key_env:
        cfg_api_key = os.getenv(cfg_key_env, "").strip() or None
cfg_api_mode = str(task_config.get("api_mode", "")).strip() or None
```

This mirrors the same `key_env`/`api_key_env` fallback pattern already used in `_fallback_entry_api_key()` and named custom provider resolution.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 15.5 (Apple Silicon M4 Max)
- Config: `auxiliary.vision.provider: custom` with `key_env: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`

items.body:
## Bug: _lineage_root_id not set on uncompressed tips, breaking desktop dedup

### Description
`_lineage_root_id` is only set during compression projection (when a root is projected to its tip). Sessions that were never compressed have no `_lineage_root_id`, so the desktop's lineage dedup in `mergeSessionPage` (`session.ts:199-209`) treats each as its own lineage. This means sessions with the same title base but no compression history appear as separate entries.

### Root cause
`hermes_state.py` lines 3857-3882: `project_compression_tips` only sets `_lineage_root_id` when replacing a root with its tip. Uncompressed sessions are returned as-is without the field.

### Fix
For every surfaced row in `list_sessions_rich`, set `_lineage_root_id` to the compression root of that chain (walk `parent_session_id` while parent `end_reason == 'compression'`), not only when projecting root to tip.

### Environment
- Hermes Agent 0.18.2
- File: `hermes_state.py` lines 3857-3882
- Related: `apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts` lines 199-209

items.body:
## Bug: Session switching is slow - no client-side transcript cache (stale-while-revalidate)

### Description
Switching between sessions in the desktop app is noticeably slow compared to Claude/ChatGPT desktop apps, which feel instant. Every session switch discards the current transcript and re-fetches the entire message history from the backend over a network call, even for sessions that were viewed seconds ago. This significantly affects usability, especially when working across 3-4 sessions.

### Root cause
Every session switch triggers two parallel network round-trips:

1. **REST prefetch**: `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` — opens SQLite, runs `SELECT * FROM messages WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY id`, serialises every row to JSON, ships over HTTP. No caching layer (`web_server.py:10118`, `hermes_state.py:4347`).

2. **Gateway RPC**: `session.resume` — rebinds the agent runtime to the target session, re-instantiates MCP servers, rebuilds system prompt, reconciles message history (`use-session-actions/index.ts:622`).

The frontend **discards** the current session's messages on every switch. There is no `Map<sessionId, ChatMessage[]>` keeping transcripts warm. The `sessionStateByRuntimeIdRef` cache (`use-session-state-cache.ts`) tracks per-session *state* (busy, turn timer, model metadata) but **not the message transcript itself**. Switching back to a session viewed 10 seconds ago re-fetches the entire transcript from SQLite.

### Contrast with Claude / ChatGPT desktop apps
- Both keep a client-side LRU cache of `sessionId → message[]`
- Switching to a previously-viewed session is a synchronous memory read — zero network calls
- Transcript fetched from server only on first load or when new messages arrive via push
- Virtualised message lists render 1000+ messages without re-measuring off-screen items

### Performance impact
- First load of a 500+ message session: 500ms-2s (SQLite read + JSON serialise + HTTP transport + React render)
- Back-and-forth switching between 2-3 sessions: same delay every time, no cache hit
- The gateway resume RPC adds further latency on top (MCP discovery, prompt build) — already parallelised with the prefetch but still blocks the "ready to type" state

### Proposed fix
Implement a stale-while-revalidate transcript cache on the frontend:

1. **Client-side LRU cache**: `Map<sessionId, ChatMessage[]>` with a configurable max size (e.g. 10 sessions). On session switch, immediately paint the cached transcript if present (synchronous — instant). Then revalidate with the REST prefetch in the background, diffing and updating only if changed.

2. **Pre-warm recently-active sessions**: The code already has a "lazy resume" path for watch windows (`use-session-actions/index.ts:622`, `lazy: true`). Extend this to pre-warm the 2-3 most recently active sessions in the background after a switch completes, so the next switch is a cache hit.

3. **Optimistic paint on first load**: For sessions not in cache, show a skeleton/loading state immediately rather than leaving the previous session's transcript visible until the new one arrives.

4. **Keep the gateway RPC async**: The `session.resume` RPC can stay non-blocking — it should not gate the transcript paint. The code already parallelises it with the prefetch; ensure the UI never waits for the RPC to complete before showing messages.

### Key files
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts:600-680` — session switch handler, fires prefetch + resume
- `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts:398` — `getSessionMessages()` REST call, no cache
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-state-cache.ts` — caches session *state* but not transcripts
- `apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts` — multi-session view state, no message cache
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/incremental-external-store-runtime.ts` — message repository, rebuilt on every switch
- `hermes_cli/web_server.py:10118` — REST endpoint, raw SQLite query per request
- `hermes_state.py:4347` — `get_messages()`, no in-memory cache

### Environment
- Hermes Agent 0.18.2
- Desktop app (Electron)

<!--
FILE ON: 2026-07-19, OR first env-class merge, OR maintainer invitation - whichever first.

HELD - nothing filed, nothing pushed, nothing public until trigger.
Local branch: feat/check-encoding-safety (LOCAL ONLY) tip 41a4117ac9e271293d16cc76dc0b5efc1c82fbeb
C-jobs fix: filed as PR #66609 (head 12b378c78), required CI green; issue #66607
-->

# Proposal: encoding-safety lint (sibling of `check-windows-footguns`)

## Summary

**Shipped evidence first.** The env-class cluster is not hypothetical:

- **#66607 closed, #66609 merged to main via salvage #66825
  (2026-07-18), authorship preserved (51e1fb8fb).** UTF-8 BOM in
  `jobs.json` crashes `load_jobs` (`JSONDecodeError` → `RuntimeError:
  Cron database corrupted and unrepairable`). Four readers fixed to
  `utf-8-sig`. The salvage itself widened the fix to three additional
  readers (backup.py, curator_backup.py, prompt_builder.py context
  scan). This checker still flags residual prompt_builder sites on the
  hit list (prompt_builder.py:1401 and prompt_builder.py:1858),
  demonstrating the class is live and the checker's coverage is real.
- **Three open fix PRs** on the same user-writable encoding/write class:
  **#65124** (dotenv BOM first-key drop), **#66475** (UTF-16 sanitize
  rewrite), **#66483** (unquoted `.env` values with spaces). **#66609**
  (jobs.json BOM crash above) is closed; merged to main via salvage
  **#66825** (2026-07-18), authorship preserved (`51e1fb8fb`).
- **Accepted-class #57247** / fix #57249 - installer writes unquoted
  `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` into `.env` (spaced paths break shell
  source). Same file family Hermes users edit by hand.
- **CONTRIBUTING already documents the Windows/Notepad BOM provenance**
  (Cross-Platform Compatibility - file encoding):

  > Config files (`config.yaml`) may be saved with a UTF-8 BOM by Notepad…
  > use `encoding="utf-8-sig"` when reading files that could have been
  > touched by a Windows GUI editor.

Users edit `~/.hermes/` state with ordinary editors (Notepad, PowerShell
5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`, VS Code). The same class keeps recurring
across independent loaders. This PR lands a **cheap opt-in lint** -
`scripts/check-encoding-safety.py` - calibrated on the six known instances;
it flags reintroduction at review time and surfaces residual sites.
House style matches `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` (staged default,
`--all` / `--diff` / paths, `# encoding-safety: ok - reason` suppression,
exit 0/1, stdlib-only AST).

Implementation footprint (vs upstream/main @ d59b79fad): 16 files, +1700/-0 -
script (+1120), tests (+168), 14 fixtures. No CI, pyproject, or docs in
this PR.

## Rule set

| Rule | Pattern | Fix |
|------|---------|-----|
| **R1** | `open()` / `read_text()` / `load_dotenv()` / `dotenv_values()` with `encoding="utf-8"` (not `utf-8-sig`) on a **user-writable** path | `encoding="utf-8-sig"` |
| **R2** | `except UnicodeDecodeError` → re-decode as `latin-1` without stripping `codecs.BOM_UTF8` | Strip BOM before latin-1; prefer utf-8-sig primary |
| **R3** | `errors="replace"` read of a user-writable file whose result is written back to disk | BOM-sniff (UTF-32→UTF-16→UTF-8); refuse-to-mangle; never persist U+FFFD |

### User-writable allowlist (explicit config, not a heuristic)

Derived from `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md` Directory Structure
plus managed-scope admin files:

**Basenames:** `.env`, `.op.env`, `config.yaml`, `config.yml`, `auth.json`,
`SOUL.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `SKILL.md`, `plugin.yaml`, `plugin.yml`,
`jobs.json`

**Path fragments / var hints:** `memories/`, `skills/`, `cron/`, `env_path`,
`config_path`, `soul_path`, `skill_md`, `jobs_file`, …

False-positive scope is a deliberate allowlist edit - not an implicit
path heuristic.

## Class table - six known instances (calibration)

| # | Site | Pre-fix shape | Issue / status | Rules |
|---|------|----------------|----------------|-------|
| 1 | `env_loader` primary | `load_dotenv(..., encoding="utf-8")` | #65123 / fix #65124 OPEN | R1 |
| 2 | `env_loader` fallback | `except UnicodeDecodeError` → `latin-1` without BOM strip | #65123 / #65124 OPEN | R2 |
| 3 | `send_cmd._load_hermes_env` | same primary+fallback on private loader | #65123 sweeper ask / in #65124 | R1+R2 |
| 4 | `_sanitize_env_file_if_needed` | `utf-8-sig` + `errors=replace` → rewrite | #66474 / fix #66475 OPEN | R3 |
| 5 | `save_env_value` / quote read context | plain utf-8 (historical) / `errors=replace` rewrite | related; utf-8-sig landed; R3 residual | R1/R3 |
| 6 | `managed_scope._cached_read` | `open(..., encoding="utf-8")` on managed `.env`/`config.yaml` | parked (scope guard on #65124) | R1 |

**Gate 1 (calibration):** 6/6 historical fixtures flagged; 0 findings on
fixed forms; suppression honored; **22/22 tests green**.

## Repo-wide run on current `upstream/main`

Base: `d59b79fadd1e9edd7afc5c679cc3b143838e7c01`  
Command: `python scripts/check-encoding-safety.py --all`  
**85 hits** across 786 scanned files: **R1=79, R2=2, R3=4**.

Update 2026-07-18: re-run on current main (`c78aa0bad`, post-#66825): **81 hits / 791 files (R1=75, R2=2, R3=4)**. The delta is the salvage resolving flagged sites (`cron/jobs.py:868 [R1]`, `cron/jobs.py:874 [R1]`, `hermes_cli/dump.py:170 [R1]`, `hermes_cli/status.py:532 [R1]`); the class shrinking because fixes merged is this checker working as intended.
Update: 85/808 @ 614dc194e (root-module scan gap fixed per sweeper review; +4 hits are newly-visible top-level modules). -> 97/850 @ bd6437d60 (rebase only, no rule changes)

Further class evidence (2026-07-18): #66994 (P0,
platform/windows) - scripts/install.ps1 ships
BOM-less UTF-8 with non-ASCII string literals;
Windows PowerShell 5.1 decodes BOM-less scripts as
ANSI, the em-dash misdecodes into a smart-quote
delimiter, and the installer fails to parse. A
community reporter independently connected it to
this proposal. Scope note: the step-1 checker is
Python-AST only and does not scan .ps1 - a
non-ASCII-literal source rule for shipped scripts
is a distinct sibling check in the same class - a
natural ladder addition once the maintainers settle
the install.ps1 invariant (BOM vs. ASCII-purity,
see #67021). Happy to build that rule if wanted.
The targeted P0 fix is #67021 (ASCII-only
install.ps1 + regression test), separate from this
proposal.

### Known limitation (recall boundary)

The checker binds path expressions to the
user-writable allowlist by name (basenames,
fragments, variable hints, loader-function names).
Opaque locals defeat this: the two sibling readers
#66825 widened to (hermes_cli/backup.py
_count_cron_jobs, agent/curator_backup.py
_backup_cron_jobs_into) read jobs.json through
bare 'path'/'src' variables and were not flagged,
even though jobs.json is in declared scope. This
is a deliberate precision-first tradeoff: binding
opaque names requires assignment tracing, which is
follow-on analysis depth (ladder, alongside the CI
step), not day-one scope. Verified against the
pre-#66825 tree: the checker scans both files
clean before and after the salvage.


### Classification (hardened 2026-07-17)

Every hit is A/B/C. **C rows require throwaway-`HERMES_HOME` runtime
evidence through the real code path**, or demotion to B with reason.
An inflated C table is worse than a shorter one.

| Class | Count | Meaning |
|-------|------:|---------|
| **A** Known/documented residual | 24 | Checker validation - env-class open work + known memory BOM issue + provider plugin residuals |
| **B** Benign | **49** | Internal/external paths, PyYAML-tolerant config, skill content with separate BOM handling, **+ 3 demoted from C after failed behavioral proof** |
| **C** Verified candidate | **12** | User-writable content, unsafely decoded, with captured runtime evidence (or upstream-ack same-class for C-memory) |

Original Gate-2 pass classified C=15. Hardening re-ran 14 C proofs
(C-memory excluded - upstream-ack); **3 demoted to B**. Remaining
**C = 11 proven + 1 C-memory corroboration = 12**.

#### A - known residuals the checker must see

- `hermes_cli/env_loader.py` L156 R1, L157 R2, L192 R3, L392 R1 - #65124 / #66475
- `hermes_cli/send_cmd.py` L245 R1, L246 R2, L268 R1 - #65124; **UTF-16 still residual** on this private loader (no sanitize path)
- `hermes_cli/managed_scope.py` L100 R1 - parked
- `hermes_cli/memory_setup.py` L94, L388 R1 - residual setup/env writer
- `hermes_cli/config.py` L7699/7822/7907 R3 - `sanitize_env_file` / `save_env_value` / `remove_env_value` rewrite shape
- `tools/memory_tool.py` L692 R1 - validates filed #10878
- Provider plugins: `hindsight`, `openviking`, `mem0`, `supermemory` env/config readers/writers - residual note on #66483

#### B - benign (why) - precision examples

These show the checker’s **precision**, not only recall: hits that look
like R1 on paper but have no user-visible BOM failure mode.

- **`config.yaml` + `yaml.safe_load`:** PyYAML accepts a leading UTF-8 BOM and
  still returns the correct root keys (verified in throwaway `HERMES_HOME`).
  Still guideline-noncompliant per CONTRIBUTING, but not the silent-key-drop
  class. Bulk of gateway/cli config readers land here.
- **External tools:** Qwen CLI auth path (`auth.py`), Codex `config.toml`
  (`codex_models.py`), docker rebootstrap seed - not HERMES_HOME user state.
- **Skill content reads:** many paths feed frontmatter parsers that
  independently `lstrip("\ufeff")` (skills_hub, blueprints); security scanner
  does not key-load.
- **Writes with `encoding="utf-8"`:** correctly not flagged (read-only R1).
- **Demoted from C (2026-07-17 hardening):**
  - `hermes_cli/doctor.py:704` - `_has_provider_env_config` uses substring
    match (`key in content`); BOM'd `OPENAI_API_KEY=…` still reports OK.
    Evidence: `content[:40]='\ufeffOPENAI_API_KEY=…'; _has_provider_env_config=True`.
  - `hermes_cli/config.py:906` - `_ensure_default_soul_md` read is plain utf-8
    but `is_legacy_template_soul` / `_normalize_soul` already `lstrip("\ufeff")`;
    custom personas preserved; legacy+BOM still upgrades.
  - `hermes_cli/doctor.py:1188` - persona non-empty heuristics still true under
    BOM; doctor reports "persona configured", not empty/missing.

#### C - verified candidates (runtime evidence)

Platform for all proofs unless noted: **darwin / Darwin 25.5.0 / Python 3.11.15 /
Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)** (verified live this session; throwaway
`HERMES_HOME`; real call sites). BOM issues hit any OS when the file was
authored on Windows or by a BOM-writing tool.

| Hit | Subclass | Severity | Verbatim evidence | User-visible impact | Dedupe / status |
|-----|----------|----------|-------------------|---------------------|-----------------|
| `agent/secret_scope.py:173` | C-env | **High** | `load_env_file keys=['\ufeffOPENAI_API_KEY', 'OTHER_KEY']; OPENAI_API_KEY in secrets=False` | Profile secret scope misses canonical API key name → auth looks missing | #65123 class; distinct call site |
| `tools/skills_tool.py:213` | C-env | **High** | `skills_tool.load_env() keys=['\ufeffOPENAI_API_KEY']; OPENAI_API_KEY in=False` | Skill env loader drops first key; skill-scoped keys look unset | #65123 class |
| `hermes_cli/dump.py:35` | C-env | Medium | `_dotenv_key_names()=['SECOND', '\ufeffOPENAI_API_KEY']; 'OPENAI_API_KEY' in names=False` | Support dump under-reports configured credentials | #65123 class |
| `hermes_cli/main.py:845` | C-env | Medium | `_has_any_provider_configured()=False; parsed keys=['\ufeffOPENAI_API_KEY']` | Provider/setup detection false-negative on BOM'd first key | #65123 class |
| `cron/jobs.py:868` | C-jobs | **High** | `RuntimeError: Cron database corrupted and unrepairable: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM …` / inner `JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM (decode using utf-8-sig)` | Cron fails to load jobs store | **#66607 closed; #66609 merged via salvage #66825 (2026-07-18), authorship preserved (51e1fb8fb)** |
| `cron/jobs.py:874` | C-jobs | **High** | same; `strict=False` re-open also fails with `JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM` | Auto-repair cannot recover | **#66607 closed; #66609 merged via #66825** |
| `hermes_cli/dump.py:170` | C-jobs | Medium | `_cron_summary(home)='(error reading)'` | Dump cron line becomes error string | **#66607 closed; #66609 merged via #66825** |
| `hermes_cli/status.py:532` | C-jobs | Medium | `display='(error reading jobs file)'; exception='JSONDecodeError: Unexpected UTF-8 BOM…'` | Status Scheduled Jobs section errors | **#66607 closed; #66609 merged via #66825** |
| `agent/prompt_builder.py:1850` | C-soul | Medium | `load_soul_md()='[BLOCKED: SOUL.md contained potential prompt injection (invisible_unicode_U+FEFF). Content not loaded.]'` | Agent persona replaced by BLOCKED warning | related invisible-unicode; distinct from #10878 |
| `hermes_cli/web_server.py:13637` | C-soul | Medium | `content[:40]='\ufeffYou are dashboard soul.\n'; starts_with_FEFF=True` | Dashboard SOUL API returns BOM-tainted content; edit round-trip can re-persist | same soul family |
| `plugins/memory/retaindb/__init__.py:517` | C-soul | Medium | `seed content[:40]='\ufeffYou are retaindb soul.'; startswith_FEFF=True` | RetainDB agent-identity seed includes leading U+FEFF | same soul family |
| `hermes_cli/doctor.py:1215` | C-memory | Medium | **Upstream-acknowledged same-class** (not re-proven this round) | Memory size/health path plain utf-8 on `memory_file` | **dedupe #10878 / #10879 / #53833** |

### C behavioral proof snippets (throwaway HERMES_HOME)

```text
# C-env (secret_scope / dotenv class)
.env = EF BB BF + "OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-test\n"
load_env_file → keys {'\ufeffOPENAI_API_KEY': ...}
canonical OPENAI_API_KEY absent  → auth fails as "missing key"

# C-jobs (crash class - fix staged on fix/cron-jobs-bom-read)
cron/jobs.json = EF BB BF + "[]"
load_jobs() → RuntimeError(... Unexpected UTF-8 BOM ...)
utf-8-sig → OK

# C-soul
SOUL.md = EF BB BF + "You are …"
load_soul_md() → [BLOCKED: SOUL.md … invisible_unicode_U+FEFF]

# send_cmd-UTF16 residual (class A validation, not new C)
.env = FF FE + UTF-16-LE "DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=…"
utf-8-sig errors=replace → U+FFFD-prefixed garbage (no sanitize on send_cmd)
```

## Guideline-compliance angle

CONTRIBUTING already mandates `utf-8-sig` for Windows-touched config.
The checker makes that checkable for the allowlisted user-writable set,
and extends the same discipline to `.env` (where PyYAML's BOM tolerance
does **not** apply - dotenv and line parsers preserve U+FEFF on the key).

## Smaller-ask ladder (rollout)

Prefer a low-friction land, then ratchet:

1. **Opt-in script first (this PR)** - land `scripts/check-encoding-safety.py`
   + fixtures + tests only. Docs wiring (CONTRIBUTING / scripts README) is
   a follow-on alongside the CI step, not in this PR. Developers and CI
   *may* run the script; **not** a required check yet.
2. **Targeted C fixes** in parallel (C-jobs crash first - filed as
   #66607 / fix #66609; C-env next; C-soul coordinated with
   invisible-unicode owners; C-memory dedupe #10878).
3. **CI gate as the follow-on** - once env-class A residuals clear and C
   crash/high sites are fixed, add:

```yaml
# e.g. in lint.yml - follow-on PR, not day one
- name: Encoding safety
  run: python scripts/check-encoding-safety.py --diff origin/main
```

- Default PR mode: `--diff` against base (noise-bounded).
- Nightly / full audit: `--all`.
- Suppressions: `# encoding-safety: ok - reason` on the same line.
- Do **not** fail the tree on day one at the current hit count (~80).

## Non-goals

- Not rewriting all 85 sites in one PR.
- Not filing the remaining C's from this proposal in the lint PR
  (C-jobs is a separate crash-class filing).
- Not changing runtime behavior in the lint PR itself.

## Test plan

```bash
uv run pytest tests/scripts/test_check_encoding_safety.py -q
# Gate 1: 22 passed; 6/6 historical fixtures flagged; fixed forms clean

python scripts/check-encoding-safety.py --list
python scripts/check-encoding-safety.py --all
# Classification: A=24 / B=49 / C=12 (hardened); none unknown

# Footguns on the lint script itself (explicit path - default is staged .py only)
python scripts/check-windows-footguns.py scripts/check-encoding-safety.py
# → no footguns, 1 file scanned, exit 0 (2026-07-18)
```

## Platforms tested

- **macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0 arm64), Python 3.11.15** - real Gate 1 (22/22)
  + full-tree `--all` (85/786) + C-proof runtime evidence above.
- **Windows** - reasoned only: `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py
  scripts/check-encoding-safety.py` clean (exit 0); the lint script itself has
  no OS-specific code paths (AST/stdlib-only; `pathlib` + allowlist path
  fragments). Not re-run on a native Windows host in this PR.

## Held asset pointer

- **Lint branch (this proposal):** `feat/check-encoding-safety` @ `41a4117ac`
  (**LOCAL ONLY** - not pushed; file on trigger below).
- **C-jobs fix (separate PR, already filed):** #66609 head `12b378c78`,
  required CI green; issue #66607. Archive bodies in
  `upstream-drafts/cron-jobs-bom-*.md`.
- Proposal path: this file
- **Trigger: FILE ON: 2026-07-19, OR first env-class merge, OR maintainer
  invitation - whichever first.**

items.title: bug(desktop): session branch creates unlinked orphan — no parent_session_id, no history copy

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Description

Desktop GUI session branching ("分支" button in the sidebar) creates a completely standalone session with **no database link** (`parent_session_id` is NULL) and **no conversation history copied** from the parent. This is functionally equivalent to `/new`, not `/branch`.

### Expected behavior

1. `parent_session_id` in the new session row should point to the parent session ID
2. The full conversation transcript from the parent should be copied into the new session
3. This should match CLI `/branch` (`/fork`) behavior

### Actual behavior

- Both sessions have `parent_session_id` = NULL in SQLite
- New session starts with a fresh user message, zero history carried over
- No `branched_from` metadata anywhere in the DB

### Evidence (from state.db)

```
Session                              parent_session_id   messages
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
20260715_202143_5566fb  (parent)     NULL                7779
20260718_110212_79421b  (branch)     NULL                  29
```

First message in the "branch" is a brand-new user prompt, not the parent transcript:

```
user | 我测试了一下，在当前冻结复制的方式...  (fresh message)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open any long-running session in Hermes Desktop
2. Right-click the session in sidebar → click "分支" (Branch)
3. Send a message in the new session
4. Check `state.db`: `SELECT id, parent_session_id FROM sessions WHERE id IN ...`

### Impact

Users expect branching to preserve context (like CLI `/branch`), so they can explore a tangent without losing the conversation state. The current desktop behavior silently discards all context and creates an orphan, which is confusing and differs from the documented CLI behavior.

### Related

- #40950 (Desktop fork-from-message — different UX path, same underlying issue)
- #65410 (Desktop branch operation silently lost on backend restart)
- #31233 (`/split` CLI feature request — references the correct branch logic)

## Blocker report: Slack reconnect loop when default gateway lacks SLACK_APP_TOKEN

### Symptom
The default Hermes gateway repeatedly logs:

```text
ERROR hermes_plugins.slack_platform.adapter: [Slack] SLACK_APP_TOKEN not set
INFO gateway.run: Reconnect slack failed, next retry in 300s
```

This keeps the gateway in a reconnect loop and causes the Dan blockers cron collector to report `has_blockers=true` even when mission boards are otherwise clear.

### Evidence
- `/Users/jasonbarbee/.hermes/logs/gateway.log` shows the error every ~5 minutes for multiple hours.
- Process table shows two gateways: default `python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace` and profile-specific `python -m hermes_cli.main --profile dan gateway run --replace`.
- `~/.hermes/profiles/dan/.env` has active `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`; `~/.hermes/.env` did not before local repair.
- Gateway restart from inside a gateway job is blocked by Hermes guard: `Blocked: cannot restart or stop the gateway from inside the gateway process`.

### Local mitigation applied
Copied the active Dan profile `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` into the global `~/.hermes/.env` and validated a fresh `load_hermes_dotenv()` sees it. Existing default gateway process still needs an external restart or hot env reload path to pick it up.

### Requested durable fix
Add a gateway startup/config guard or profile-aware Slack env loading path so a profile gateway can either:
1. load profile `.env` for Slack adapter credentials when launched with `--profile`, and/or
2. emit an actionable diagnostic that names the missing env file and restart requirement.

A self-restart from within a cron/gateway job is correctly blocked, but the blocker collector needs a clean way to distinguish "env repaired; restart pending" from an active unresolved config error.

items.title: session_search fails with 'database disk image is malformed' while hermes sessions repair reports clean

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

`session_search` returns `database disk image is malformed`, but `hermes sessions repair --check-only` reports the DB as healthy. This leaves users with no official repair path.

## Reproduction

1. Have a `state.db` with partial FTS5 index corruption (e.g. after interrupted migration / WAL contention).
2. Run `hermes sessions repair --check-only` → `opens cleanly — no repair needed`.
3. Run any operation that uses `session_search` (or call `tools/session_search_tool.py` directly) → `database disk image is malformed`.

## Root cause

`hermes sessions repair` relies on `_db_opens_cleanly()` which only runs `PRAGMA integrity_check`, a basic `sessions` read, and a single rolled-back FTS write probe. It does not exercise the actual FTS5 queries used by `session_search`, so partial index corruption (e.g. bad `messages_fts*` shadow table segments) slips through undetected.

This matches the orphan-shadow-table scenario described in #56815: the virtual table definition exists, but internal FTS5 data is corrupt, causing `MATCH + ORDER BY rank` / snippet queries to fail while simple `SELECT` still works.

## Impact

- `session_search`, `/resume` title resolution, and any feature relying on FTS5 discovery are permanently broken.
- The official repair tool gives false confidence.
- Users must either drop to raw SQLite surgery or live without session recall.

## Suggested fixes

1. Extend `_db_opens_cleanly()` to run representative FTS5 queries (`MATCH`, `rank`, `snippet`) and detect partial corruption.
2. Add a `--force-rebuild-fts` flag to `hermes sessions repair` (or a separate `hermes sessions repair --fts` mode) that drops and recreates `messages_fts*` / `messages_fts_trigram*` from `sqlite_master`, then backfills from `messages`.
3. Consider making Strategy 0 of `repair_state_db_schema()` more aggressive when FTS5 is present but unhealthy.

## Workaround (manual, zero data loss)

Replace `$HERMES_HOME` with your actual Hermes home directory (usually `~/.hermes`):

```bash
DB="${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/state.db"

# Backup
cp "$DB" "$DB.backup.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"

# Drop all FTS5 schema entries
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3, os
db = os.path.expandvars("${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/state.db")
conn = sqlite3.connect(db, isolation_level=None)
conn.execute('PRAGMA writable_schema=ON')
conn.execute("DELETE FROM sqlite_master WHERE name LIKE 'messages_fts%'")
conn.execute('PRAGMA writable_schema=OFF')
conn.execute('VACUUM')
conn.close()
PY

# Let Hermes recreate FTS5 virtual tables
python3 -c "from hermes_state import SessionDB; db = SessionDB(); db.close()"

# Rebuild indexes from canonical messages table
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3, os
db = os.path.expandvars("${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/state.db")
conn = sqlite3.connect(db, isolation_level=None)
for idx in ('messages_fts', 'messages_fts_trigram'):
    conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO {idx}({idx}) VALUES('rebuild')")
    conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO {idx}({idx}) VALUES('optimize')")
conn.close()
PY
```

## Related

- #56815 — FTS5 virtual table schema loss orphans shadow tables
- #33865 — state.db FTS corruption goes undetected

## Environment

- Hermes version: current main (2026-07-18)
- SQLite with FTS5 enabled
- Triggered by interrupted migration / WAL contention under concurrent CLI + gateway writes

items.title: [Bug]: Pre-update snapshot skips state.db due to hardcoded 1 GiB limit — no rollback path for large DBs

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Description

After commit d0dcb9a5fd (`fix(update): consolidate pre-update backups into one gated mechanism`, merged Jul 16), `hermes update` adds a hardcoded 1 GiB file size cap to the pre-update snapshot via `_PRE_UPDATE_SNAPSHOT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1 << 30`.

When `state.db` exceeds this limit, the file is skipped with a warning:

```
⚠ Snapshot: skipping state.db (1.7 GB exceeds 1.0 GB limit)
```

The update completes, but `state.db` is excluded from the pre-update snapshot. If the update fails or corrupts state, there is no clean rollback path.

## Context

- `state.db` size on this system: **1.7 GB**
- The 1 GiB limit was added to prevent the snapshot from stalling on very large DBs (the commit notes an observed case of 24 GB). That is a valid concern.
- However, the current implementation hard-fails the snapshot inclusion with a warning rather than offering a fallback path (e.g. skip only the large DB file, snapshot the rest, and optionally require the user to manually back up the DB beforehand).

## Expected Behavior

- Users with `state.db` > 1 GiB should receive a clear warning before the update
- The pre-update snapshot should still capture pairing configs, cron jobs, auth, etc. (it does, which is correct)
- Either: (a) a config flag to explicitly include large DBs with acknowledgment, or (b) documentation that users with large DBs must run a manual `cp state.db` before updating

## Impact

- Users with active Hermes deployments accumulate large `state.db` files over time (root cause: trigram FTS index bloat — see #55233)
- For these users, `hermes update` now silently leaves them without a state rollback path
- This is a regression from pre-d0dcb9a5fd behavior, where the snapshot included `state.db` regardless of size

## Related Issues

- #55233 (open) — trigram FTS index causes state.db bloat to multi-GB within weeks
- #58672 (open) — pre-update snapshot uses `keep=1`, silently prunes all other quick snapshots
- #35376 (closed) — /tmp staging bug for large DB backups

### Problem

The `session_search` tool currently supports FTS5 text search, but there is no way to narrow results by date range. The CLI has `hermes sessions list --older-than N` and `hermes sessions prune`, but the in-session `session_search` tool is a different entry point and does not expose any temporal filtering.

### Use case

I often remember that a conversation happened around a specific day or week (e.g. "the cron issue I debugged last Tuesday" or "that MCP config fix from early July"). Today I have to search by keyword and then scroll through results to find the right timeframe, which is slow and imprecise.

### Proposed behavior

Add optional date/time filters to the `session_search` tool (and matching UI/CLI parity), e.g.:

- `from` / `since` — ISO date/datetime or relative duration (`1h`, `7d`, `2026-07-01`).
- `to` / `until` — same formats.
- `on` — single calendar day shortcut.
- Result ranking should still apply, but only return messages whose timestamp is inside the window.

Ideally this uses the existing `created_at` / message timestamp column already present in `state.db` (see related work in #40476).

### Prior art / related

- CLI: `hermes sessions list --older-than N`, `hermes sessions prune`
- Issue #40476: "fix(session_search): use match message timestamp instead of session creation date for 'when' field" — date-aware rendering is already being discussed there, so filter logic should probably reuse the same timestamp field.

### Would you like to implement this?

No, filing as a user request.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop exits without confirming detached updater spawn or early process survival

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

**Affected component:** Desktop update handoff

The Desktop update path spawns a detached updater, immediately calls `unref()`, and quits the Electron app after a fixed 2.5-second dwell. The handoff does not observe asynchronous child-process `error` events or early `exit` events, so a failed/short-lived updater can leave the desktop app closed without enough evidence to diagnose whether it was never spawned, failed to exec, or exited immediately.

Severity suggestion: **Medium — reliability and diagnosability**.

A historical macOS incident had this visible result: the user confirmed an update, the desktop app exited, no updater appeared, and the app did not relaunch. A later controlled update completed normally, so this report does **not** claim a specific historical errno, exit code, or signal.

## Environment

Confirmed on the inspected installation:

- Hermes Agent 0.18.2
- Hermes Desktop 0.17.0
- Electron 40.10.2
- macOS arm64

## Relevant code paths and call chain

- `apps/desktop/src/app/updates-overlay.tsx`
  - Update confirmation invokes the update action.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/updates.ts`
  - The update action crosses the Desktop bridge.
- `apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts`
  - IPC bridge forwards the request to the Electron main process.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`
  - Prepares the update handoff, releases the backend lock, constructs updater arguments, and requests process creation.
  - Schedules unconditional `app.quit()` after `UPDATE_HANDOFF_DWELL_MS` (2.5 seconds).
- `apps/desktop/electron/updater-process.ts`
  - `spawnUpdaterProcess()` calls `spawn()` and then `child.unref()`.
  - The returned child wrapper exposes only `pid` and `unref`; it does not retain or observe `error`, `spawn`, or `exit`.

The process is intentionally detached with ignored stdio. That is reasonable after a verified handoff, but leaves no Desktop-side evidence if startup fails before the updater's own logging becomes available.

## Observed successful timeline

A later controlled update completed with this sanitized relative sequence:

- T+0: updater child was created.
- T+2.5 s: Desktop exited; the updater remained alive/reparented.
- T+~52 s: update work completed and Desktop relaunched.

This proves the normal path can work. It does not reproduce the historical failed handoff or reveal its errno/signal.

## Why the failure is hard to diagnose

Node may report executable/start failures asynchronously through the child `error` event. A detached process may also exit before the fixed dwell expires. In the current sequence:

1. `spawn()` is called.
2. The child is immediately unreferenced.
3. An update marker is written from the PID.
4. Desktop quits after 2.5 seconds regardless of whether the updater reached a stable running state.

As a result, the UI can disappear before an asynchronous failure is observed, and the update marker may imply a handoff that never became viable. The existing updater logs cannot help if the updater never successfully begins writing them.

## Expected behavior

- Desktop should only exit after a bounded, explicit handoff-success condition.
- Spawn failure or early updater death should leave Desktop running (or recover its backend state) and show a clear error.
- A marker should not survive as evidence of a successful handoff when the same updater fails before it is viable.
- Logs should capture enough redacted lifecycle metadata to distinguish failure classes.

## Suggested minimal design

This is a design direction, not a mandate for a final architecture:

1. In `spawnUpdaterProcess()`, register `spawn`, `error`, and `exit` listeners immediately, before any `unref()`.
2. Use a bounded settle window (the existing 2.5 seconds is a reasonable upper bound) to treat either a `spawn` event plus survival or a clear error/early-exit result as the handoff outcome.
3. Write/update the handoff marker only after spawn is confirmed; make marker cleanup ownership-aware.
4. On failure, keep Desktop open or restore the backend lifecycle, and return a structured IPC result for a user-visible error.
5. On success, detach/unref and schedule Desktop exit exactly once.
6. Emit redacted lifecycle records containing timestamp, executable identity, sanitized argument shape, PID, errno/code, exit code, and signal. Do not record environment values, tokens, credentials, or full command-line secrets.

The Windows recovery path should follow the same observable contract.

## Test cases requested

- `ENOENT` / missing updater executable.
- `EACCES` / non-executable updater.
- Updater exits non-zero before the settle window.
- Updater exits due to a signal before the settle window.
- Updater survives the window and Desktop exits once.
- Marker is written once and cleared only by its owner on failure.
- Backend recovery path is invoked on failed handoff.
- No duplicate quit or duplicate updater occurs under IPC retries.

## Impact

This is primarily a reliability and diagnostics gap. It can strand a user with Desktop closed and no clear update state even though the underlying cause may be recoverable. The report deliberately does not attribute the historical incident to a particular OS error because that evidence was not captured.

No local paths, PIDs, user data, credentials, environment values, or full logs are included.

items.title: [Bug]: _interim_assistant_visible_text crashes on multimodal (list) content — "expected string or bytes-like object, got 'list'"

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Traceback

run_agent.py:4824 → _interim_assistant_visible_text(previous_msg)
→ _strip_think_blocks(content or "") → re.sub(list) → TypeError


## Root Cause
When the API returns multimodal content (list of `{type:"text"}, {type:"image_url"}` parts), `_interim_assistant_visible_text()` passes the raw list to `_strip_think_blocks()`, which does `re.sub()` on it. Lists aren't strings → `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'list'`.

The `content or ""` fallback doesn't help because a non-empty list is truthy.

## Fix
Flatten multimodal content to a string before passing to `_strip_think_blocks`:

\`\`\`python
if isinstance(content, list):
    text_parts = []
    for part in content:
        if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get("type") == "text":
            text_parts.append(str(part.get("text", "")))
        elif isinstance(part, str):
            text_parts.append(part)
    content = " ".join(text_parts) if text_parts else ""
\`\`\`

items.body:
# [Desktop]: Close (×) button on most modal panels does nothing — umbrella report (3 panels affected)

> **Status:** Drafted 2026-07-18 by judy167.
> **Submission blocker:** Same as `desktop-session-to-workspace-jump.md` — GitHub PAT lacks `repo` / `public_repo` scope, so `gh issue create` will fail with `Resource not accessible by personal access token (createIssue)`.
> **Workaround:** Widen PAT scope (Settings → Developer settings → PAT → Regenerate with `public_repo` ticked), then `gh issue create --body-file H:/hermes/github-issues/desktop-modal-close-button-dead.md`, or paste the body block at https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/new .

## Title

```
[Desktop]: Close (×) button on most modal panels does nothing — umbrella report (3 panels affected)
```

## Body

```markdown
## Summary

In the Hermes Desktop app (Windows, v2026.7.7.2), the **×** close button in the top-right corner of most modal / overlay panels is non-functional. Clicking it does not dismiss the panel. This affects at least the three panels below — likely the same root cause across all of them, so I'm filing as a single umbrella so maintainers can fix once at the right layer.

Symptoms are identical across all three:
- Cursor changes to a pointer on hover, so the button **looks** clickable.
- Click registers (no "dead pixel" feel) but the panel does not close.
- No animation, no error toast, no log line in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\gui.log`.
- Workaround that always works: press **Esc**, or click outside the panel's content area. (Click-outside also fails on some panels — see §3.)
- Modal stays on top of all other windows until dismissed via Esc.

## Affected panels (so far)

### 1. New Project / New Workspace creation modal
- **Trigger:** Click the `+` in the sidebar, or `project_create` from chat.
- **Fields inside:** Name input, Path picker.
- **× behavior:** Dead. Esc works.

### 2. Settings / Preferences (top-level) panel
- **Trigger:** Settings gear icon in sidebar / header.
- **Fields inside:** Model provider, profile selector, theme, etc.
- **× behavior:** Dead. Esc works.

### 3. Settings sub-panels (e.g. MCP server config, Model provider edit)
- **Trigger:** Clicking a row inside the Settings panel to drill in.
- **Fields inside:** Varies (form fields, toggles, key-value editors).
- **× behavior:** Dead. **Esc works, but click-outside does NOT close this one** — you have to find the `×` to get back to the parent settings panel, which compounds the issue.

## Motivation

This is a small bug with a disproportionately large annoyance factor. Every time I want to dismiss one of these panels I instinctively reach for `×`, it does nothing, and I have to remember to press Esc instead. Over a day of use that's dozens of micro-frustrations. More importantly, the **dead button actively misleads users** into thinking the app is hung or that their click didn't register, so they click again — sometimes twice — which on form panels (§3) has been observed to submit the underlying form with partial data.

The fact that **click-outside fails on §3** is the part that pushes this from "cosmetic" to "actually broken UX": the user has no escape hatch except keyboard, which is hostile to mouse-only users and bad for discoverability.

## Proposed behavior

- The **×** button on every modal/overlay should dismiss the panel, period.
- **Esc** should keep working as a keyboard escape (already works — preserve it).
- **Click-outside** should dismiss on every modal, not just some. (Either intentionally gate it on §1, where data-loss risk exists if the user has typed a name — fine — but in §3 there's no data-loss risk so it should just work.)
- While the user is hovering the **×**, show the standard "click to close" cursor (already works) **and** a tooltip `Close (Esc)` so the keyboard alternative is discoverable.

A clean implementation would be a single shared `Modal` / `Overlay` component with one wired-up close handler, rather than each panel reimplementing it (which is almost certainly why the bug exists — three panels, three slightly different close wiring, three ways for the close to be forgotten).

## How to reproduce

```text
1. Launch Hermes Desktop on Windows 10.
2. (Panel §1) Click the `+` in the sidebar → modal appears → click × in top-right → modal stays.
3. Press Esc → modal closes (control case).
4. (Panel §2) Click the settings gear → panel appears → click × → panel stays.
5. Press Esc → panel closes.
6. (Panel §3) From settings, click any row to drill in (e.g. MCP config) → sub-panel appears → click × → sub-panel stays.
7. Try clicking outside the sub-panel → still stays.
8. Press Esc → sub-panel closes.
```

## Expected vs actual

| Panel | Action | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| New Project | Click × | Closes | Stays open |
| Settings | Click × | Closes | Stays open |
| Settings sub-panel | Click × | Closes | Stays open |
| Settings sub-panel | Click outside | Closes (no unsaved state) | Stays open |

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop v2026.7.7.2 (latest release as of 2026-07-18)
- Windows 10
- Logs: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\gui.log` shows no entries when × is clicked — confirms the click is being eaten client-side before reaching any handler.
- Repro is deterministic — happens every time, on all three panels.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] × closes every modal/overlay panel.
- [ ] × behavior is consistent across all panels (single source of truth).
- [ ] Esc continues to work as a backup dismiss.
- [ ] Click-outside behavior is consistent: either enabled everywhere it is safe (e.g. settings sub-panels) or explicitly disabled everywhere it is unsafe (e.g. forms with unsaved input — show a confirmation dialog instead of dismissing silently).
- [ ] × button gets a tooltip `Close (Esc)` for keyboard-shortcut discoverability.
- [ ] A test / lint rule ensures any new modal added in the future must wire the close button (catches the regression pattern).

## Related

- None filed yet from my side. If maintainers prefer one issue per panel instead of this umbrella, I'm happy to split — just say the word.
```

---

## Re-submit steps

```bash
# Option A: widen the PAT scope (github.com → Settings → Developer settings → PAT
# → Regenerate with `public_repo` ticked), then:
gh issue create \
  --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent \
  --title "[Desktop]: Close (×) button on most modal panels does nothing — umbrella report (3 panels affected)" \
  --body-file H:/hermes/github-issues/desktop-modal-close-button-dead.md

# Option B: paste the body block above into the browser at
# https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/new
```

items.title: Gateway test suite has real-world side effects: speaks through the developer's TTS and launches real Chrome
items.body:
## Summary

Running the stock gateway test suite on a Windows dev machine (real Chrome installed, TTS provider configured) produces two surprises:

1. **The machine speaks out loud** — the literal phrase *"partial answer complete"* is synthesized via the developer's real configured TTS provider and played through the speakers, once per suite run.
2. **Real headed Chrome windows pop up** — `chrome.exe --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=<pytest tmp>\...\chrome-debug`, once per suite run (3/3 runs, deterministic).

Command observed:

```
python -m pytest tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py tests/test_lazy_session_regressions.py tests/tui_gateway
```

on `main` @ `c48d53413`, Windows 10, Python 3.11.

## Mechanism 1: TTS env-var pollution escapes monkeypatch

The chain:

- `tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py:1140` does `monkeypatch.delenv("HERMES_VOICE_TTS", raising=False)` and then calls the RPC `voice.toggle action=tts`.
- The handler mutates the process environment directly — `tui_gateway/server.py:14247`: `os.environ["HERMES_VOICE_TTS"] = "1" if new_value else "0"`.
- `monkeypatch` only restores changes made *through monkeypatch*. The handler's direct `os.environ` write is invisible to it, so `HERMES_VOICE_TTS=1` **leaks to every subsequent test in the process**.
- Later, `test_session_activate_returns_inflight_stream_before_completion` (`tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py:7809`) completes a fake agent turn whose scripted reply is `"partial answer complete"` (line 7831). The turn-completion path at `tui_gateway/server.py:9740` sees `_voice_tts_enabled()` true and dispatches the string to the **real** `hermes_cli.voice.speak_text` on a daemon thread — real synthesis, real audio.

Suggested fix: an autouse fixture in the gateway test suite that snapshots/restores `HERMES_VOICE` / `HERMES_VOICE_TTS` (or pins them to `"0"`), plus a mock on `speak_text` at the dispatch site so no test can ever reach a real provider.

## Mechanism 2: a connect-path test reaches the real Chrome launcher

Each suite run spawned one real Chrome: `--remote-debugging-port=9222`, with `--user-data-dir` under pytest's tmp basetemp — i.e. the test had `HERMES_HOME` pointed at a pytest tmp dir (so `chrome_debug_data_dir()` resolved there), but the launcher itself was **not** patched, and with a real Chrome binary on PATH the launch succeeds and the window stays up after the suite exits (leaks until manually killed).

Most `browser.manage connect` tests patch `launch_chrome_debug` / `try_launch_chrome_debug` / `get_chrome_debug_candidates`; at least one path escapes on Windows with Chrome installed. The timing places it in `tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py`'s browser section (~lines 8160–8440). CI presumably never sees this (headless runners without Chrome-on-PATH, `get_chrome_debug_candidates` returns empty), which is why it survives.

Suggested fix: an autouse fixture for the browser-connect test block that patches `get_chrome_debug_candidates` to `[]` (spawn becomes impossible by construction), so an unpatched code path fails an assertion instead of launching a browser.

## Why it matters

Beyond the jump-scare factor, both side effects are state leaks: the TTS pollution can flip assertion outcomes in later voice-related tests depending on shard composition, and the leaked Chrome holds port 9222, which can then interfere with the very `browser.connect` behavior other tests exercise.
