items.body:
## Bug Report

**Environment:** Discord gateway, Hermes Agent (latest)

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. While Hermes is working on a task in Discord DM
2. Use `/queue` with an attached image
3. The image is not passed through to the queued prompt

**Expected:** Images attached with `/queue` should be included when the queued prompt is processed, just like they are in normal messages.

**Actual:** The image is silently dropped. Only the text portion of the queued message is processed.

**Context:** User wanted to queue a message with a screenshot while the agent was mid-task. The text went through but the image was lost.

**Suggested Fix:** The queue handler in the gateway should preserve any attachments/images from the original message and replay them when the queued prompt is executed.

items.title: computer_use cannot follow cua-driver's verify/escalate ladder

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes currently cannot follow cua-driver's documented **verify → escalate** ladder.

cua-driver already reports machine-readable action outcomes such as `verified`, `effect`, `code`, `degraded`, and `escalation.recommended`, and its input tools support per-call `delivery_mode: "background" | "foreground"`. Hermes's wrapper:

1. drops those structured action outcomes,
2. exposes no `delivery_mode` to the model,
3. injects background-only guidance that conflicts with the current driver contract, and
4. uses process-global backend/approval state despite concurrent Hermes sessions.

This causes the agent to report success for suspected/unverified no-ops, conclude that cua-driver fundamentally cannot operate some Electron/Chromium surfaces, or reach for external foreground shims even though cua-driver already exposes a bounded foreground rung.

This is a cross-platform Hermes integration issue. It was observed while testing the Linux TLDraw Offline Electron app, but the contract mismatch applies to macOS and Windows too.

## Original Linux/Electron symptom

During a TLDraw Offline test, a background click did not dismiss the script-consent dialog or interact with the renderer. Hermes concluded that cua-driver could not deliver clicks to Electron and proposed `xdotool`.

The more accurate result should have been:

1. try the background AX/PX rung,
2. preserve the driver's structured outcome,
3. re-snapshot and verify,
4. if the result reports `background_unavailable`, `effect: "suspected_noop"`, or `escalation.recommended: "foreground"`, let the model explicitly request the foreground rung,
5. ask for approval because foreground briefly changes focus,
6. repeat the same action once and verify the UI changed.

Electron should not itself be a heuristic for foreground: different controls and delivery paths in the same application behave differently.

## Verified Hermes gaps

Audit performed against `main` at `5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d`.

### 1. Structured action outcomes are discarded

[`ActionResult`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/tools/computer_use/backend.py#L70-L81) carries only `ok/action/message/capture/meta`.

[`CuaDriverBackend._action()`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/tools/computer_use/cua_backend.py#L2313-L2335) computes:

```python
ok = not out["isError"]
```

and builds `meta` from `out["data"]` only. It ignores `out["structuredContent"]`.

[`_text_response()`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/tools/computer_use/tool.py#L464-L470) then returns only `ok/action/message/meta`.

This collapses materially different outcomes:

- confirmed
- delivered but unverified
- suspected no-op
- refused/background unavailable
- failed

An unverified action is not necessarily a failure, but it also must not be presented as confirmed success.

### 2. Foreground is not model-reachable

The [public schema](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/tools/computer_use/schema.py#L16-L233), backend interface, and [dispatcher](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/tools/computer_use/tool.py#L356-L455) expose no `delivery_mode`.

The adapter's click/drag/scroll/type/key methods therefore cannot pass it to cua-driver.

Hermes advertises `focus_app(raise_window=true)`, but the adapter [explicitly ignores `raise_window=True`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/tools/computer_use/cua_backend.py#L1968-L1980). Persistent `bring_to_front` and bounded per-call foreground delivery should remain separate concepts.

### 3. Hermes guidance is background-only and stale

Hermes has two instruction layers:

- hard-coded guidance automatically injected whenever `computer_use` is enabled,
- a bundled `computer-use` skill available through the skills system.

The [hard-coded system guidance](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/agent/prompt_builder.py#L481-L592) promises absolute background operation.

The [bundled skill](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/skills/computer-use/SKILL.md#L20-L34) likewise says all actions run in the background, and its click-no-effect guidance only says to recapture/check for a modal.

The canonical cua-driver skill pack is optional (`cua-driver skills install`) and is not installed by `hermes computer-use install`. Even when present, it documents raw cua-driver controls that the Hermes wrapper currently hides.

### 4. Foreground/result state must be session-local

[`tools/computer_use/tool.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/tools/computer_use/tool.py#L139-L168) caches one backend and approval state process-wide.

[`CuaDriverBackend`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/5988fe6cd5547d3620df1de889ac6007f5463b4d/tools/computer_use/cua_backend.py#L1179-L1217) holds sticky active PID/window, snapshot tokens, and one cua-driver session id. Its comment assumes one Hermes run equals one backend, which is not true for a gateway serving concurrent sessions.

Any "last action recommended foreground" gate or approval cache must be per conversation/run, not another process-global variable.

## Why the model, not the driver, selects foreground

cua-driver should own the platform mechanics and evidence:

- attempt the exact requested rung,
- detect known delivery limitations,
- return `verified/effect/code/escalation`,
- activate and restore the previous foreground when explicitly requested.

Hermes should own transport normalization, approvals, and session isolation.

The model should compare the driver result and post-action snapshot with the semantic task goal, then select the next rung.

Do **not** silently auto-retry foreground in the adapter. The first action may have landed but remained unverifiable; an automatic retry could double-submit, double-click, increment twice, or confirm something twice. Foreground is also a user-visible focus change and needs explicit authorization.

This is the key difference from the automatic fallback proposed in #57623.

## Proposed implementation

### Phase A: preserve the result contract

- Extend `ActionResult` or introduce a first-class outcome/status that preserves:
  - `verified`
  - `effect`
  - `code`
  - `escalation`
  - `degraded`
  - delivery path/mode
- Normalize `structuredContent` in `CuaDriverBackend._action()`.
- Keep `isError` as transport/tool failure information; do not treat it as the full semantic verdict.
- Surface optional fields additively in the model-facing response.
- Add regression tests for confirmed, unverifiable, suspected-noop, background-unavailable, degraded, and old-driver/no-structured-content responses.

### Phase B: expose bounded foreground delivery

- Add optional `delivery_mode: "background" | "foreground"` to the existing `computer_use` schema for input actions.
- Default to background.
- Pass it through the backend interface and CUA adapter.
- Inspect advertised tool input schemas or a formal capability token before sending it. Do not probe old drivers by sending an unknown field; they may silently ignore it.
- If foreground is requested but unsupported, return a structured `foreground_unsupported` result with an update hint.
- Route foreground through approval that explicitly says it will briefly change focus.
- Scope approval by both action and delivery mode; background approval must not silently authorize foreground.
- Do not add a separate foreground tool and do not expose raw CUA MCP tools.

### Phase C: update guidance and isolate state

- Change both the system prompt and bundled skill from **background-only** to **background-first**.
- Teach the evidence-driven AX → PX → foreground ladder.
- Document that `foreground` is a reaction to a real signal, not a prediction based on Electron/GTK/Chromium.
- Keep permission dialogs, secrets/passwords, payments, 2FA, and destructive actions stop-and-ask.
- Make backend target state, result history, and approval state conversation/run-scoped.
- Clarify how the canonical cua-driver skill pack is installed/discovered and remove stale references to the planned Hermes autodetection and renamed skill files.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Hermes preserves and returns cua-driver's structured action verdicts.
- [ ] `effect:"unverifiable"` is distinguishable from both confirmed success and failure.
- [ ] The model can request `delivery_mode:"foreground"` on supported input actions.
- [ ] Foreground is rejected unless explicitly selected and approved; there is no hidden automatic retry.
- [ ] Old drivers fail clearly when foreground is requested rather than silently executing background.
- [ ] Background remains the default.
- [ ] System guidance and the bundled skill describe the same evidence-driven ladder.
- [ ] Result history, active target, snapshot tokens, and approval state do not leak across concurrent Hermes runs.
- [ ] Linux TLDraw/Electron smoke test: background attempt → structured escalation/no-op evidence → approved foreground retry → post-action verification.
- [ ] Tests cover Windows/macOS/Linux-shaped structured responses without requiring raw CUA tools to be model-facing.

## Related work

- #57623 — Windows background failures and hidden foreground control. Overlaps, but proposes automatic fallback; this issue proposes explicit model-selected escalation.
- #59731 / #59755 — unverified action handling and first-class status.
- #47072 — tracking issue for decoupling the Hermes wrapper from cua-driver internals.
- #55048 — earlier foreground-dispatch work for a subset of actions.

The narrow-waist architecture should remain: one Hermes `computer_use` tool, with a thin, lossless adapter over cua-driver's documented contract.
